name: Things That Go Bump
blurb: Glimmer Falls was built on top of a lot of yesterdays, and on Halloween week they all want to say hello. Porch lights blink, buses that stopped running in 1958 make one more stop, and the junkyard forgets how to end.

encounters.title: The Endless Lot
encounters.place: Rusty's Junkyard, somewhere past midnight
encounters.text: You blink on your own front lawn and open your eyes between two rusted station wagons. This is Rusty's Junkyard, except the rows of cars never end. Every car is the same wood-paneled wagon, every radio is on, and every radio is playing the same slow-dance ballad from the 1959 prom, "Moonlight on the Quarry," one beat out of sync, forever.
encounters.art: A teenager in pajamas standing in an endless junkyard maze of identical rusted wood-paneled station wagons stretching to the horizon under a full moon, every dashboard radio glowing the same amber, mist between the rows

choices.label: Follow the song to wherever it is loudest

success.text: The ballad swells, row after row, until you reach the car crusher. Its radio is the only one playing the song on the right beat. You click it off. Silence rolls outward like a wave, the rows fold away like a deck of cards, and you are standing at the junkyard gate with the stars where they belong.
success.art: A teenager reaching into the cab of a car crusher to switch off a glowing radio, rows of identical station wagons folding away behind them like playing cards, the junkyard gate ahead under starlight

failure.text: The song gets louder, then closer, then inside your head. The nearest radio dial glows like a cat's eye and the needle swings toward you. You lean in to turn it off and the static grabs you by the collar and pulls you straight through the speaker grille. The night is not done with you yet.
failure.art: A teenager being pulled face-first into the glowing speaker grille of a station wagon dashboard radio, streams of amber static wrapping around them, endless identical cars behind

choices.label: Hotwire a wagon and drive straight through the rows

success.text: Two wires, one spark, and the engine coughs awake. You floor it down the aisle and the identical cars peel aside like curtains. The radio finally changes stations on its own, to KGLM, and you roll to a stop in your own driveway with the headlights off and the engine still ticking.
success.art: A wood-paneled station wagon bursting out of a misty junkyard maze with headlights blazing, rows of identical cars parting like curtains, a suburban driveway glowing ahead

failure.text: The engine catches, the wheel turns itself, and the wagon drives you in a slow, polite circle around the same three rows while the ballad plays on. You wake in its back seat at dawn with a seatbelt buckled across you that you never fastened.
failure.art: A teenager asleep in the back seat of a station wagon at dawn, a seatbelt buckled over them, the steering wheel turning by itself, a junkyard misty and gray outside

choices.label: Scratch an X on every car you pass

success.text: On the fortieth car you find your own X already waiting. It is a loop. So you look for the one car without a mark, the one that smells like motor oil instead of old perfume. Its back door opens onto the junkyard office, and there is a coffee can of loose change under the seat.
success.art: A teenager pointing at a single unmarked station wagon among dozens scratched with X marks, its back door open onto a lit junkyard office, a coffee can of coins on the seat

failure.text: Every car you reach already has an X on it. Hundreds of them, then thousands, all scratched in your handwriting, some of them rusted over as if you made them years ago. You stop scratching. The radios keep playing.
failure.art: An endless row of identical station wagons each scratched with the same X, some old and rusted, a teenager staring at their own key in their hand

encounters.title: Yes, No, Goodbye
encounters.place: A wood-paneled basement rec room on Crystal Street
encounters.text: Somebody brought a Spirit-Talk board from the Starlight Mall toy store, and the slumber party has been giggling over it for an hour. Then the planchette moves before anyone touches it. It spells your name. Then it spells OPEN THE DOOR, and the door to the garage starts to rattle in its frame.
encounters.art: Teens in sleeping bags around a talking board on shag carpet in a wood-paneled basement rec room, the planchette sliding by itself, the garage door rattling in the background, a lava lamp glowing

choices.label: Ask the spirit, politely, who it is

success.text: P-A-T-T-Y. She was twelve. Her own slumber party got rained out in 1960 and she has been waiting ever since. You let her play one round of light-as-a-feather, and everyone swears their fingers lifted. The planchette glides to GOODBYE, and the garage door goes still.
success.art: Teens in a circle doing light as a feather in a candlelit basement, a faint glowing girl in a 1960 nightgown laughing among them, the talking board planchette resting on goodbye

failure.text: The planchette spins like a top, flies across the room and sticks in the wood paneling. Every sleeping bag zips itself shut, with people still in them. When you get them unzipped, there is a cold print of a small hand on your wrist that will not warm up until morning.
failure.art: A plastic planchette stuck in wood paneling, sleeping bags zipped shut and squirming on a basement floor, a frosty small handprint glowing on a teenager's wrist

choices.label: Slam the planchette onto GOODBYE

success.text: You slap the planchette down on GOODBYE so hard the board bends. The lights snap on, the furnace kicks in, and the garage door is just a garage door again. The board is cardboard and a price sticker. Somebody laughs, and then everybody does.
success.art: A teenager slamming a hand down on a talking board's goodbye with the overhead lights flaring on in a basement rec room, friends startled then laughing

failure.text: The planchette pushes back with the strength of a grown-up. It drags your hand across the letters, H-E-R-E, and the garage door bangs open on an empty, dark garage where the bicycles are all spinning their wheels.
failure.art: A dark open garage with every bicycle's wheels spinning by themselves, a teenager's hand dragged across a talking board in the foreground

encounters.title: Porch Light Code
encounters.place: Crystal Street, two in the morning
encounters.text: You wake up because your room keeps flashing. Outside, every porch light on the cul-de-sac is blinking in perfect unison: long, short, short, long. No one is awake. No one is on the porches. The pattern stops, starts over, and waits, like somebody repeating a question.
encounters.art: A suburban cul-de-sac at 2 a.m. with every porch light blinking in unison, a teenager silhouetted in an upstairs bedroom window, the roundabout garden dark in the middle

choices.label: Write the blinks down and decode them

success.text: Dots and dashes fill your notebook. L-O-O-K U-N-D-E-R M-A-T. Under your own doormat is a 1944 silver dollar and a note in faded pencil: Thank you for noticing us. Every porch light gives one warm, long blink and goes out for the night.
success.art: A teenager kneeling at a front door holding a silver dollar and a faded pencil note found under the doormat, porch lights along the street glowing warm gold

failure.text: You get as far as R-U-N before every porch light goes dark at once. Then one light comes back on. It is not on a porch. It is your bedside lamp, behind you, and you did not leave it on.
failure.art: A dark cul-de-sac with every porch light out, a single bedside lamp glowing in a teenager's bedroom behind them as they stare out the window

choices.label: Flash your own light back and answer

success.text: You blink back H-I. The street goes still. Then, one by one, the porch lights spell H-I back, slow and happy, like old neighbors waving from across the years. A dog howls somewhere, cheerful, and the lights settle into a soft, ordinary glow.
success.art: A teenager on a lawn aiming a flashlight at a row of porch lights that glow warm and friendly in reply, ghostly outlines of 1950s neighbors waving from the porches

failure.text: Your flashlight bulb pops with a sound like a cap gun. Every porch light on the street swivels on its bracket to point at you, and they stay pointed until sunrise, warm on the back of your neck no matter where you stand.
failure.art: Porch light fixtures on every house twisted on their brackets to aim at one teenager on a dark lawn holding a dead flashlight

encounters.title: Candles at Pinecrest
encounters.place: Pinecrest Cemetery, after the gates are locked
encounters.text: A line of people in old-fashioned clothes is walking between the headstones, each one carrying a candle that does not flicker in the wind. Bonnets, fedoras, a girl in a poodle skirt. The last one in line turns, smiles, and holds out a spare candle to you.
encounters.art: A silent procession of translucent figures in clothes from many decades carrying steady candles between moonlit headstones, the last figure offering a candle to a teenager behind a mausoleum

choices.label: Take the candle and walk with them

success.text: You walk with them to the cemetery gate. They are the town's forgotten dead, heading out for the one Halloween they never got. At the gate they each say their name to you, and you say yours back. The candle stays lit in your hand all the way home and never melts.
success.art: A teenager walking at the end of a ghostly candlelit procession through an open cemetery gate, the figures turning to say their names, warm candlelight on the teen's face

failure.text: The candle gets heavier with every step until it weighs as much as a brick. The procession files into a mausoleum and the iron door swings shut with you inside. The groundskeeper lets you out at dawn and does not ask a single question.
failure.art: A teenager pressed against the bars of a mausoleum door at dawn, an extinguished candle at their feet, a groundskeeper with a ring of keys approaching

choices.label: Duck behind a headstone and count them

success.text: You count forty-eight. The forty-eighth stops, tips his fedora in your direction, and keeps walking. You were seen, and you were let be. On the headstone you hid behind, someone has left a tarnished subway token and a peppermint.
success.art: A ghostly man in a fedora tipping his hat toward a headstone where a teenager hides, a tarnished token and a peppermint resting on the stone

failure.text: Forty-eight. Forty-nine. Fifty. There is one more every time you start over. When you finally reach the end of the line, the last candle is not in front of you. Its warmth is on the back of your neck.
failure.art: A teenager crouched behind a headstone counting on their fingers, a candle glowing directly behind their head held by a pale hand

encounters.title: The Last Bus
encounters.place: Corner of Crystal Street and Quarry Road, three a.m.
encounters.text: A round-nosed yellow school bus from the fifties idles at the corner where no bus has stopped in decades. The sign says GLIMMER FALLS ELEMENTARY: FIELD TRIP. The doors fold open with a sigh. Inside, a busload of kids in saddle shoes and cardigans press their faces to the windows and wave at you.
encounters.art: A 1950s round-nosed yellow school bus idling at a foggy suburban corner at 3 a.m., doors open, translucent kids in saddle shoes waving from every window, the driver's face hidden under a cap

choices.label: Climb aboard and ask where the field trip goes

success.text: The kids scoot over to make room. The field trip goes everywhere: the old drive-in, the soda fountain, the quarry beach before it was drained. They sing the whole way. At dawn the bus drops you at your door and a girl hands you a felt pennant that reads I WENT.
success.art: A teenager riding a glowing 1950s school bus full of singing ghost kids past a vintage drive-in theater, a felt pennant being handed over the seat

failure.text: The doors close and the bus drives you all over town. Every stop is your house, but wrong: painted a different color, a different car in the driveway, a different family in the window. It lets you off at sunrise in your pajamas, three blocks from home.
failure.art: A teenager in pajamas stepping off a ghostly school bus at sunrise onto an unfamiliar version of their own street, a house painted the wrong color

choices.label: Wave back and keep your feet on the curb

success.text: You wave with your whole arm. The kids light up and wave harder. The doors fold shut, the bus pulls away, and its taillights break apart into a swarm of fireflies that drift up over the rooftops of Crystal Street.
success.art: A teenager waving from the curb as a ghostly school bus pulls away, its red taillights dissolving into a swarm of fireflies rising over suburban rooftops

failure.text: You raise your hand and every kid on the bus stops waving at once. They all turn to look past you, at your house, and they keep looking as the bus rolls away, until it is gone around a corner that is not there in daylight.
failure.art: A row of ghost children on a school bus all turned to stare at a single suburban house, a teenager frozen on the curb with one hand raised

encounters.title: Footsteps in the Attic
encounters.place: Your house, 1:13 a.m.
encounters.text: Somebody is pacing in the attic. Back and forth, back and forth, right above your bed, in hard-soled shoes. Your family is asleep. Then the pull-down ladder in the hallway creaks, unfolds itself step by step, and lands softly on the carpet like an invitation.
encounters.art: A dark suburban upstairs hallway with an attic pull-down ladder unfolding by itself, a faint light and the shadow of pacing feet visible through the ceiling hatch

choices.label: Climb the ladder with a flashlight in your teeth

success.text: Up in the attic, an electric train set from 1959 is running on its own, around a little papier-mache Glimmer Falls with tiny painted houses. A boy's voice whispers, "Nobody ever came up to see it." You stay and watch three full laps. The train slows, happy, and stops at the station.
success.art: A teenager in a dusty attic watching a vintage electric train circle a papier-mache model town, flashlight beam catching floating dust, a faint boy's silhouette kneeling beside the tracks

failure.text: The ladder folds up behind you with a bang and the hatch latches. In the pitch dark the pacing stops, and then starts again, right next to you. You spend the night sitting on a box of Christmas ornaments until somebody downstairs wonders why the ladder is stuck.
failure.art: A teenager hugging their knees on a box of Christmas ornaments in a pitch-black attic, the faint outline of shoes pacing beside them in a sliver of light

choices.label: Talk to the ceiling like an old roommate

success.text: "Hey. Rough night?" The pacing stops. Then two taps: yes. You talk for an hour about school and records and who you have a crush on, and the taps answer. In the morning there is a 1950s quarter on your pillow, polished bright.
success.art: A teenager lying in bed talking up at the ceiling at night, a soft glow through the plaster above, a shiny old quarter resting on the pillow beside them

failure.text: The footsteps stop. Then they start running, back and forth, faster and faster, and the attic hatch rattles in its frame like someone pounding to get out. It goes on until the sky turns gray and your alarm clock goes off.
failure.art: An attic hatch in a dark hallway rattling violently in its frame, dust raining down, a frightened teenager peeking out from their bedroom door

name: The Body Count
blurb: Every October somebody in a rubber mask decides Glimmer Falls needs a sequel. Babysitters, roller rinks, pumpkin patches and empty high-school hallways: the rules are the rules, and the rules say never split up.

encounters.title: Have You Checked the Children?
encounters.place: The Delgado house, 9 Crystal Street, 11:40 p.m.
encounters.text: You are babysitting the Delgado twins for five dollars an hour and a fridge full of Bolt Cola. The kids are asleep. The phone has rung three times. Each time it is the same slow breathing, and then a voice like a rake on gravel: "Have you checked the children?" This time it adds, "Nice socks."
encounters.art: A teenager on a shag carpet clutching a wall phone with a long curly cord in a dim split-level living room, a babysitter's note on the fridge, the dark staircase to the bedrooms behind them

choices.label: Go upstairs and check the children

success.text: The twins are asleep, but their window is open and there is a muddy bootprint on the sill. You slam the window, lock it, and stand guard with a lamp in one hand. Outside, a shape backs off across the lawn. The next time the phone rings, it is just a click.
success.art: A teenager slamming a child's bedroom window shut, twin kids asleep under rocket-ship blankets, a muddy bootprint on the sill and a shadowy figure retreating across a lawn outside

failure.text: The twins are fine, but the closet door is open one inch and there is something standing very still behind the coats. You drag a dresser in front of it and sit there with a lamp. When the Delgados get home at one, they find you in the hall, and the closet is empty.
failure.art: A teenager sitting in a dark hallway with a table lamp raised like a club, a dresser shoved against a closet door, parents in party clothes appearing at the top of the stairs

choices.label: Call the operator and keep the voice on the line

success.text: The operator traces it to the payphone outside the Quik-Mart on Quarry Road. You call the sheriff, then watch from the window as a cruiser's lights sweep the booth. A tall figure hangs up, drops the receiver, and walks away into the trees. It does not call again tonight.
success.art: A payphone booth outside a convenience store at night lit by a sheriff cruiser's red and blue lights, a tall masked figure walking away into the trees, the receiver dangling

failure.text: "Honey," the operator says, after a long pause, "that line was disconnected in 1971." On the other end, very close to the mouthpiece, the breathing turns into a slow, delighted laugh.
failure.art: A teenager pale with fear holding a phone receiver away from their ear, a disconnected-line notice taped to an old phone on the kitchen wall

choices.label: Bundle the twins out the back to the one porch light still on

success.text: You carry one twin and drag the other in a sleeping bag across three back lawns to the only porch light on the street. Grandma Pearl is already up, rocking, a shotgun full of rock salt across her knees. "Sit," she says, and nothing follows you. She sends you home with a coffee can of salt.
success.art: A teenager hauling two sleepy kids across dark backyards toward a glowing porch where an elderly woman rocks with a rock-salt shotgun across her knees

failure.text: The back door will not open. Something in the yard knocks on the glass, three slow knocks. You hustle the twins into the bathtub with every pillow in the house and sing them commercial jingles until dawn.
failure.art: A teenager and two small kids huddled in a pink bathtub piled with pillows, a shadowy hand pressed against a frosted bathroom window

encounters.title: The Last One Standing
encounters.place: Glimmer Falls High, after the lights go out
encounters.text: You only came back for your backpack. The hall lights die one bank at a time, and at the far end of the trophy hallway a figure in janitor's coveralls and a grinning homecoming-king mask lifts a pair of hedge trimmers. Snip. Snip. Every slasher movie you have rented says the same thing: run.
encounters.art: A long high-school hallway in darkness, rows of lockers, a figure in janitor's coveralls and a grinning homecoming-king mask holding hedge trimmers at the far end, a teenager with a backpack frozen in a pool of emergency light

choices.label: Sprint the long hallway for the gym doors

success.text: You hit the push bar at full speed and burst into the gym. You slap every light switch on the panel and yank the fire alarm. Lights blaze, bells scream, sprinklers rain. When you turn around, the doorway is empty except for a dropped pair of hedge trimmers.
success.art: A teenager bursting into a high-school gym under blazing lights and spraying sprinklers, a fire alarm handle pulled down, abandoned hedge trimmers on the threshold

failure.text: The hallway is longer than it should be. Lockers slam shut one after another behind you, getting closer. You dive into an open locker and pull it shut. The janitor finds you there at six in the morning and lets you out without a word.
failure.art: A teenager peering out through the slats of a high-school locker in a dark hallway, a long shadow with hedge trimmers passing outside

choices.label: Duck into the chem lab and improvise

success.text: Baking soda, vinegar, the dish soap from the sink, all in the big beaker. Foam floods the doorway just as the mask comes through. Its sneakers skid, it windmills, and it sails backward through the open window into the hedges. When you look out, the hedge is empty.
success.art: A wave of white foam spilling across a chemistry lab floor, a masked figure in coveralls slipping backward toward an open window, a teenager holding an empty beaker

failure.text: Everything you mix just goes puff in a little purple cloud. The masked figure walks calmly through the smoke, whistling, and you leave by the window yourself, landing in the rosebushes with half your jacket left behind on the latch.
failure.art: A masked figure strolling through a puff of purple smoke in a chemistry lab while a teenager scrambles out a window into rosebushes

choices.label: Grab the state championship trophy and stand your ground

success.text: You smash the trophy case, grab the 1979 softball state cup and swing. The mask cracks clean in half and falls off. There is nobody inside. The coveralls crumple to the floor like laundry, and the hedge trimmers clatter down beside them.
success.art: A teenager swinging a gold trophy cup at a masked figure, the mask splitting in half to reveal empty darkness, coveralls collapsing like laundry, glass from a trophy case glittering

failure.text: The trophy is plastic. It bounces off the mask with a hollow bonk, and the grin seems to get wider. You flee out the fire door with the alarm wailing and do not stop running until you reach the bike racks.
failure.art: A plastic trophy bouncing off a grinning homecoming-king mask, a teenager fleeing through a fire exit with an alarm light flashing red

encounters.title: Lookout Point
encounters.place: The lookout below the KGLM water tower
encounters.text: You and some friends are parked at the lookout in a borrowed car, watching the town lights and counting meteors. The radio cuts in with a bulletin about a man seen near the reservoir with a rusty garden hook. Then something on the roof of the car goes scrape. Scrape. Scrape.
encounters.art: A boxy 1980s car parked at a hilltop lookout above glittering small-town lights, teens inside staring up at the roof, a meteor streaking across the sky, a rusty hook glinting above the windshield

choices.label: Floor it down the switchbacks

success.text: Gravel sprays, everyone screams, then everyone laughs, and you fishtail all the way down Tower Road. At the bottom you get out to check the car. An old rusted garden hook is dangling from the door handle. You leave it in the ditch where it belongs.
success.art: Teens laughing in a car fishtailing down a winding hill road at night, a rusted garden hook swinging from the passenger door handle

failure.text: The engine floods and dies. The scraping slides from the roof to the trunk to the passenger door and back again, slow circles, until a pair of headlights comes up the hill and the sound stops all at once.
failure.art: A stalled car at a dark lookout, teens huddled inside, scratch marks spiraling around the car's paint, distant headlights climbing the hill

choices.label: Call the KGLM request line from the payphone and get on the air

success.text: Mix puts you on the air live. "Glimmer Falls, if you are up, flash your porch light for the kids at the lookout." Below, the whole town blinks on, hundreds of lights. Something heavy drops off your roof and crashes away into the pines, outnumbered.
success.art: A view from a hilltop lookout of an entire small town flashing its porch lights, a hulking shadow fleeing into the pine trees, a teen holding a payphone receiver

failure.text: The payphone line connects, but KGLM is only playing one sound: a slow scrape, scrape, scrape, in perfect time with the car roof. You hang up and sprint back to the car, and the scrape is still on the radio inside it.
failure.art: A teenager dropping a payphone receiver at a dark lookout, a car radio glowing behind them with sound lines in the shape of scratches

encounters.title: Last Pick of the Patch
encounters.place: Halvorsen's Pumpkin Patch, off Quarry Road, after closing
encounters.text: Every jack-o-lantern in the patch has lit itself. The scarecrow is missing from its post. From the corn maze comes the wet, patient scrape of someone carving, and then a figure steps out with a sack-cloth face, a pumpkin for a head, and a carving knife the size of a canoe paddle.
encounters.art: A moonlit pumpkin patch full of glowing jack-o-lanterns, an empty scarecrow post, a lanky figure with a carved pumpkin head and a comically huge carving knife stepping out of a corn maze

choices.label: Lose it in the corn maze

success.text: Left, left, right, double back. You hear it crash through a wall of corn and then a thump and a muffled oof as it runs straight into the hay-bale pyramid. You stroll out the exit. Behind you, a pumpkin head pokes up from the hay, looking embarrassed.
success.art: A teenager walking calmly out of a corn maze exit while behind them a pumpkin-headed figure sits buried to the neck in toppled hay bales

failure.text: The maze rearranges every time you turn a corner. Every path leads you back to the empty scarecrow post. On the fifth time, the post is not empty. It is wearing your jacket.
failure.art: A scarecrow post in a corn maze clearing wearing a teenager's jacket, the teenager stopped short in shock, corn walls leaning in

choices.label: Smash the brightest jack-o-lantern

success.text: You find the biggest, brightest, meanest-grinning pumpkin and give it a home-run swing. Every lantern in the patch goes out at once. In the dark, the pumpkin-head figure folds up like a dropped scarecrow, nothing but straw and a sack.
success.art: A teenager mid-swing smashing a giant glowing jack-o-lantern, every other lantern in the patch going dark, a scarecrow collapsing into straw behind them

failure.text: The pumpkin explodes into a geyser of seeds and orange goo that coats you from head to sneakers. Every other jack-o-lantern in the patch laughs, all at once, and the giant knife scrapes on a stone somewhere close behind you.
failure.art: A teenager drenched head to toe in orange pumpkin goo and seeds, surrounded by dozens of jack-o-lanterns with wide laughing faces

encounters.title: Lights Out at the Rink
encounters.place: The roller-rink annex at Pump Iron Gym, late skate
encounters.text: Halfway through the late skate the lights cut out, but the mirror ball keeps turning. When the emergency lights stutter on, there is one extra skater on the floor: a figure in a striped referee shirt and a yellow smiley-face mask, gliding backward, carrying a skate key the size of a crowbar.
encounters.art: A roller rink lit only by a spinning mirror ball and red emergency lights, teens on skates scattering, a masked skater in a striped referee shirt gliding backward with an oversized skate key

choices.label: Outskate it around the rink

success.text: You grab hands with every skater you pass and form a crack-the-whip, faster and faster. At the end of the line you let go and go flying out the exit doors into the parking lot. The masked skater cannot make the turn and slams into the snack bar.
success.art: A line of teens on roller skates doing crack the whip around a rink, the last skater flying out through exit doors, a masked skater crashing into a snack bar counter

failure.text: You hit a dropped Bolt Cola can and go down hard, wheels spinning. The smiley face looms over you and taps the giant key on its palm. Then the DJ brings the lights up and it is gone, but your laces have been tied together.
failure.art: A teenager sprawled on a roller rink floor with skate wheels spinning, laces knotted together, a smiley-face mask fading into the mirror-ball sparkle above them

choices.label: Reach the DJ booth and kill the music

success.text: You lift the needle off the record. The masked skater freezes mid-glide, like it is playing musical statues and cannot help it. You leave it there, frozen in the mirror-ball light, and find three quarters on the floor of the booth on your way out.
success.art: A teenager lifting a needle off a spinning record in a DJ booth, a masked skater frozen mid-glide on the rink below, quarters scattered on the booth floor

failure.text: The record changes by itself to a slow ballad. The speakers announce COUPLES ONLY. Every other skater pairs off and rolls away into the dark, leaving you alone on the floor with the smiley face and its outstretched hand.
failure.art: An empty roller rink under a mirror ball, a masked skater offering a gloved hand to a lone teenager, couples skating away into the shadows

encounters.title: Across the Street
encounters.place: Your bedroom window, after midnight
encounters.text: Someone in a pale, blank Halloween-store mask is standing under the streetlight by the roundabout, perfectly still, facing your house. You look away to grab your glasses. When you look back, it is one lawn closer. You look away again. Two lawns.
encounters.art: View from a dark teenage bedroom window over a cul-de-sac at night, a figure in a blank pale mask standing perfectly still on a neighbor's lawn under a streetlight

choices.label: Snap a picture to prove it's real

success.text: Flash. The Polaroid develops slowly: the streetlight, the lawn, and in the figure's place, a garden gnome wearing a cheap rubber mask. When you look up, the lawn is empty. The gnome is back in the Fergusons' flowerbed, and the mask is in their trash can.
success.art: A developing Polaroid photo showing a garden gnome wearing a rubber mask under a streetlight, a teenager's hand holding it by a bedroom window

failure.text: Flash. The Polaroid develops slowly: your bedroom, your back, and the mask standing directly behind you. You spin around. Nobody. When you look out the window again, the streetlight is empty too.
failure.art: A Polaroid photo showing a teenager at a window with a pale masked figure standing right behind them, the real bedroom behind the teen empty

choices.label: Wake the whole street with the phone tree

success.text: You call the Lindqvists, who call the Fergusons, who call everyone. Porch lights pop on all around the cul-de-sac. Neighbors step out in bathrobes with flashlights and garden rakes. The figure is gone. On the lawn where it stood is a dropped mask and a flattened circle of grass.
success.art: Neighbors in bathrobes stepping onto porches with flashlights and rakes all around a lit-up cul-de-sac, a dropped pale mask lying on an empty lawn

failure.text: Nobody picks up. Then your phone rings once. Then the house next door rings once, you can hear it through the wall. Then the next house closer, and the next, one ring per house, walking toward yours.
failure.art: A teenager clutching a phone in a dark kitchen while sound rings ripple from house to house down the street toward theirs

choices.label: Refuse to blink

success.text: You stare it down for twenty full minutes. Your eyes burn. Then, slowly, it takes a step backward. And another. Lawn by lawn, it retreats to the streetlight and out of the light and gone. You blink, finally, and laugh until you cry.
success.art: A teenager with wide, unblinking eyes pressed to a bedroom window while a masked figure retreats backward across lawns into the dark

failure.text: Your eyes water and close for half a heartbeat. When they open, the mask is pressed flat to your window glass, its breath fogging the pane. Then it is gone, and there is only a smudge on the outside of a second-story window.
failure.art: A blank pale mask pressed against a second-story bedroom window from outside, breath fog on the glass, a teenager recoiling

name: Creature Feature
blurb: Something slithered up from the storm drains, something hatched in the pet shop, and the hedge animals in the roundabout have started to wander. In Glimmer Falls, nature is fighting back, and it brought teeth.

encounters.title: Something in the Storm Drains
encounters.place: The storm grate at the end of Crystal Street
encounters.text: It rained all evening, and now the storm grate at the end of the street is making a sound like a giant slurping the last of a milkshake. Two round lights, the color of taillights, blink at you from down in the dark. A kid's lost sneaker on the curb slides, by itself, toward the grate and drops in.
encounters.art: A rain-slick suburban curb at night, a storm drain grate with two glowing red eyes blinking in the darkness below, a child's sneaker sliding toward it, streetlight reflected in puddles

choices.label: Lower a flashlight on a jump rope and look

success.text: The beam finds a white alligator the size of a canoe, wearing a faded Pet Paradise collar from 1979. It is not angry. It is lonely and hungry. You drop it a package of bologna. It blinks slowly, the way cats do when they like you, and slides away down the tunnel.
success.art: A flashlight beam on a jump rope lighting a huge pale alligator in a storm drain tunnel, a faded pet-shop collar around its neck, a slice of bologna falling toward its open jaws

failure.text: The rope goes taut, then yanks out of your hands. Your flashlight beam tumbles down, down, down, and then goes crunch. From the grate comes a long, satisfied burp that rattles every garbage can on the street.
failure.art: A jump rope whipping down into a storm drain, a flashlight beam tumbling into darkness, garbage cans rattling along the curb

choices.label: Pry up the grate and climb down after the sneaker

success.text: Knee-deep in cold water, you find a nest: lost sneakers, tennis balls, three Frisbees and a pile of coins, all arranged with care. It has been collecting. Something huge rumbles behind you like an outboard motor purring. You leave it a Frisbee and keep the change it offers.
success.art: A teenager knee-deep in a storm drain tunnel beside a nest of lost sneakers, tennis balls, Frisbees and coins, a huge shadowy reptile curled contentedly behind them

failure.text: The current knocks you flat and carries you through a mile of tunnels. You get spat out of a drain in the Starlight Mall parking lot at four in the morning, smelling exactly like the food court dumpsters.
failure.art: A soaked teenager crawling out of a storm drain in an empty mall parking lot at night, neon mall signs dark, a puddle of greasy water around them

encounters.title: Pets After Dark
encounters.place: Pet Paradise, lower level of the Starlight Mall, after closing
encounters.text: On a dare, you hid in the photo booth until the mall closed. Now every cage in Pet Paradise is open. The hamster wheels spin in the dark. The parakeets are whispering your name, all together. And in the aquarium aisle, something big and shaggy is eating the fish food straight out of the tubs.
encounters.art: A dark mall pet shop after hours lit by glowing aquarium tanks, every cage door hanging open, parakeets lined up on a shelf, a huge shaggy silhouette hunched over fish food tubs in the aquarium aisle

choices.label: Herd everything back into its cage

success.text: You make soft clicking sounds and the puppies follow you like a parade. The snake coils back into its tank, the parakeets hop onto their perch. The big shaggy thing turns out to be a tortoise the size of a coffee table, wearing a toupee of moss. It lets you scratch its chin.
success.art: A teenager leading a parade of puppies back to their pens in a moonlit pet shop, a coffee-table-sized tortoise with a mossy shell stretching its chin to be scratched

failure.text: The parakeets learn your name perfectly and scream it at the top of their lungs. Mall security's flashlight swings toward the shop. You hide under the fish tanks for an hour while forty birds tell the guard exactly where you are.
failure.art: A teenager hiding under a row of glowing fish tanks while a mall security guard's flashlight sweeps the store, parakeets shrieking on every perch

choices.label: Follow the crumbs to the big one

success.text: It is a guinea pig. It is a guinea pig the size of a Saint Bernard, and it is very sorry about the fish food. It squeaks, a sound like a tea kettle. You scratch behind its enormous ears, and it nudges open the service door so you can get out of the mall.
success.art: A teenager scratching the ears of an enormous fluffy guinea pig the size of a large dog in a pet-shop aisle, a service door propped open behind them

failure.text: The crumbs lead in a circle. You realize it is behind you a second before it sneezes. You are coated, head to toe, in something warm and green. You run for the dead wing and do not look back.
failure.art: A teenager drenched in green slime running through a dark mall corridor, a giant shaggy shape sniffling in a pet-shop doorway behind them

encounters.title: The Roundabout Hedges
encounters.place: The roundabout garden, Crystal Street
encounters.text: The topiary animals in the roundabout garden have moved. The hedge swan is standing in the street. The hedge poodle is on the Kowalskis' lawn, digging. The hedge rabbit is gone completely, and from the dark between the houses comes the sound of leaves rustling against siding, getting closer.
encounters.art: A suburban roundabout garden at night with empty topiary plinths, a hedge-trimmed swan standing in the street, a hedge poodle digging on a lawn, leaves rustling in the shadows between houses

choices.label: Borrow the Lindqvists' hedge clippers

success.text: Snip, snip, snip. The poodle sheds its pompoms and sits, ashamed, on the lawn. The swan honks and waddles home. The rabbit comes hopping out from behind a garage and climbs back onto its plinth on its own. By sunrise, the garden looks freshly trimmed.
success.art: A teenager with long hedge clippers trimming a topiary poodle on a lawn at night, a topiary swan waddling back toward the roundabout, a hedge rabbit climbing onto its plinth

failure.text: The privet grabs the clippers, then your sleeve, then the rest of you. You spend the night stuck in the hedge poodle like a burr, until the automatic sprinklers come on at five and it lets you go, sputtering.
failure.art: A teenager tangled inside a topiary poodle on a dark lawn, only their sneakers and one arm sticking out, sprinklers spraying at dawn

choices.label: Turn on every sprinkler on the street

success.text: You know where every spigot on the route is. One by one the lawns hiss to life. The topiaries sigh, drink, and stroll back to the roundabout like cats after dinner, settling on their plinths with their leaves glistening. The swan even fluffs itself.
success.art: Sprinklers spraying across moonlit lawns, topiary animals walking contentedly back to their plinths in a roundabout garden, leaves sparkling with water

failure.text: The water makes them grow. In minutes, the hedge swan is two stories tall and peering in your bedroom window with a leafy, curious eye. It is still there when you wake up, and the Lindqvists are going to need a ladder.
failure.art: A giant two-story topiary swan peering into a teenager's upstairs bedroom window at dawn, sprinklers still running on the lawn below

encounters.title: Something Got Out of the Clinic
encounters.place: The garage veterinary clinic, Crystal Street
encounters.text: The side door of the garage clinic is swinging open. Inside, a crate rattles on the floor, its tag reading DO NOT FEED AFTER DARK in marker. The crate is empty. From the rafters, between the Christmas decorations and the camping gear, something hisses and blinks three eyes at you.
encounters.art: A suburban garage converted into a vet clinic at night, an empty pet crate with a warning tag on the floor, three glowing eyes peering down from rafters stuffed with holiday decorations

choices.label: Coax it down with a can of tuna

success.text: It is an opossum with three eyes and a soft purple glow in its belly, and it loves tuna. It climbs down your arm, purrs like a cat, and curls up back in its crate. In the morning there is a thank-you note on your door: It likes you. Most people it bites. A.H.
success.art: A three-eyed opossum with a softly glowing purple belly eating tuna from a can in a teenager's hands in a dim garage clinic

failure.text: It drops onto your head and settles in like a hat. It refuses to leave. You run in circles in the driveway, waking every dog on the street, while it chirps happily and steers you by the ears.
failure.art: A teenager running in circles on a driveway at night with a three-eyed opossum perched on their head like a hat, porch lights flicking on

choices.label: Throw a tarp over it and grab

success.text: One throw and the tarp comes down over the whole lump. It wiggles, chirps, and gives up. You slide it back into its crate and latch it. The next day there are three dollars in quarters in your mailbox with a sketch of a three-eyed smiley face.
success.art: A teenager wrestling a wiggling tarp-covered lump into a pet crate in a garage, a stern warning tag tied to the crate

failure.text: The lump under the tarp splits into four smaller lumps, and all four scatter in different directions across Crystal Street. You hear them chirping in the hedges for the rest of the night, and one of them seems to be in your attic.
failure.art: Four small lumps scurrying out from under a tarp in different directions across a dark cul-de-sac, a teenager staring in dismay

encounters.title: The Glimmer Falls Grabber
encounters.place: The edge of Crystal Woods, behind the cul-de-sac
encounters.text: Every kid in town has heard of the Glimmer Falls Grabber: eight feet of moss and swamp hair that steals garbage cans. Tonight there are footprints across your backyard as long as a skateboard, and at the tree line something huge steps into the moonlight carrying the Fergusons' trash can like a lunchbox.
encounters.art: An eight-foot shaggy moss-covered creature at the edge of a pine forest in moonlight carrying a metal garbage can, giant footprints leading across a suburban backyard

choices.label: Get it on the camcorder

success.text: You get forty-five seconds of clear footage: the Grabber digging through the trash, finding a half-eaten birthday cake, and doing an unmistakable happy dance. It is the best monster footage anyone in Glimmer Falls has ever shot. Nobody will believe it, and that is okay.
success.art: A camcorder viewfinder showing a huge shaggy creature doing a happy dance over a half-eaten birthday cake in the woods, a red record light glowing

failure.text: You get thirty seconds of your own shaky sneakers and the sound of something breathing right above the camera. When you dare to look up, there is nothing there but a single strand of swamp hair dangling from a branch.
failure.art: A shaky camcorder view of a teenager's sneakers in pine needles, a long strand of mossy hair dangling down into view from above

choices.label: Leave it your Halloween candy stash

success.text: You set your pillowcase of candy on a stump and back away. The Grabber sniffs it, takes it gently, and leaves something in its place: a pinecone, a polished purple geode chip, and a dime from 1961. It nods once and is gone into the trees.
success.art: A tree stump in moonlight holding a pinecone, a polished purple crystal chip and an old dime, a huge shaggy figure disappearing between the pines with a pillowcase of candy

failure.text: It takes the candy. Then it takes the pillowcase, then your left sneaker, then follows you home and sits on your roof until dawn, making contented crunching sounds above your bed.
failure.art: A huge shaggy creature sitting on a suburban rooftop at night eating candy from a pillowcase, a single sneaker dangling from its hand

encounters.title: Under the Pool Cover
encounters.place: The Fergusons' backyard pool, closed for the season
encounters.text: The Fergusons are in Reno and you promised to feed their cat. The cat is missing. The green tarp over their pool is bulging in the middle, rippling, and a bubble the size of a beach ball rises under it and pops with a sound like a giant frog clearing its throat.
encounters.art: A suburban backyard swimming pool at night covered with a bulging green tarp, a huge bubble swelling under it, an empty cat bowl on the patio, a teenager with a flashlight at the gate

choices.label: Peel back the cover with the pool skimmer

success.text: Under the tarp is a frog as big as a recliner, green and gold and perfectly calm. Sitting on its head like a crown is the Fergusons' cat, also perfectly calm. The frog croaks. The cat meows. You carry the cat inside, and the frog sinks with dignity to the deep end.
success.art: A giant green and gold frog in a swimming pool with a calm house cat perched on its head like a crown, a teenager peeling back a pool tarp with a skimmer

failure.text: The tarp wraps around your ankle and drags you to the edge. Something slick and cold licks your sneaker right off your foot. You scramble back to the patio with one shoe and a lot of slime.
failure.art: A teenager scrambling backward across a pool deck with one sneaker missing, a green tarp snaking from the pool around their ankle, slime glistening

choices.label: Pull the drain valve and wait

success.text: The water gurgles away. Something big squeezes through the drain toward the creek with a long, rubbery squelch, and the Fergusons' cat leaps out from under the tarp straight into your arms. When they get home, they tip you for going above and beyond.
success.art: A pool draining in a swirling whirlpool at night, a rubbery green shape squeezing into the drain, a house cat leaping into a teenager's arms

failure.text: You turn the wrong valve. The water rises instead, the tarp pops off like a cork, and a tidal wave of green goo covers the patio, the lawn chairs and you. The cat watches from the roof, judging.
failure.art: A wave of green goo bursting out of a backyard pool over lawn chairs and a teenager, a house cat watching from a rooftop

name: Strange Skies
blurb: Up past the TV antennas, something very large and very patient has noticed Crystal Street. The stars rearrange, the late-late show signs off in a voice with too many vowels, and every grown-up on the block stares at the sky and hums.

encounters.title: The Stars Move
encounters.place: The middle of the cul-de-sac, two a.m.
encounters.text: You came out to watch the meteor shower. Instead, the stars over Crystal Street start to slide, slow and deliberate, like beads on an abacus. The Big Dipper empties itself. Orion walks off. Every TV antenna on every roof creaks around to point straight up, and the stars begin to spell something.
encounters.art: A teenager lying on a cul-de-sac lawn staring up as the stars slide into new patterns across the night sky, every rooftop TV antenna twisted to point straight up, faint lines connecting the moving stars

choices.label: Chart the new constellations in your notebook

success.text: You sketch fast. The stars make a map of Crystal Street, every house a point of light, and then, in tidy cursive across the Milky Way: WE LIKE YOUR DECORATIONS. You do not know what that means. But it does not feel like a threat, and you know the sky a little better now.
success.art: An open notebook covered in hand-drawn star charts shaped like a cul-de-sac map, a teenager looking up at stars forming looping cursive across the Milky Way

failure.text: The stars rearrange into your own handwriting. They write GO INSIDE. Then they write it again, bigger, and then the whole sky tilts like a fishbowl being turned, and you crawl back to the porch on your hands and knees.
failure.art: A night sky where the stars spell out words in a teenager's handwriting, the horizon tilting at a sick angle, a teen crawling across a lawn toward a porch

choices.label: Lie back on the lawn and refuse to be impressed

success.text: You fold your arms behind your head and yawn at the sky, loudly. The stars hesitate. Then, one at a time, they slink back to their usual places, like kids caught out of bed. The antennas creak back around. You fall asleep on the lawn, unbothered.
success.art: A teenager lying on a lawn with arms folded behind their head yawning at the sky, stars sheepishly drifting back into their familiar constellations

failure.text: The lawn starts to tilt up toward the sky, slowly, like a ramp. Lawn chairs slide past you. You dig your fingers into the grass and hold on until dawn, when gravity remembers which way it goes.
failure.art: A teenager gripping the grass of a lawn that tilts up toward a swirling starry sky, lawn chairs and a garden gnome sliding past them

encounters.title: Sign-Off
encounters.place: Your living room, after the late-late movie
encounters.text: Channel 13 is signing off: the flag, the anthem, the test pattern of circles and lines. Then a voice comes on that is not a person. It reads the name of every family on Crystal Street, slowly, kindly, with too many vowels. "Good night, Glimmer Falls," it says. "We are watching." The TV is unplugged.
encounters.art: A glowing console television in a dark wood-paneled living room showing a test pattern of concentric circles, its unplugged cord lying on the carpet, a teenager on the couch clutching a pillow

choices.label: Wrestle the channel dial to anything else

success.text: The dial fights you, clunk by clunk, and then snaps around. Every channel is suddenly showing old cartoons, a rabbit outwitting a hunter on all thirteen of them. You leave them on all night, laughing too loud, and the voice does not come back.
success.art: A teenager wrenching the channel dial of a console TV, the screen bursting into colorful classic cartoons, the living room lit warm

failure.text: Every channel is the same test pattern and the same voice, still reading names. It reaches your street address. It reaches your house. It says your name, and then it pauses, as if waiting for you to answer.
failure.art: A console TV showing concentric circles on every channel as the dial spins, a teenager frozen in front of it, sound waves curling from the speaker

choices.label: Tape it on the VCR for someone who'll believe you

success.text: You get it on tape. Played backward at double speed, the voice is singing a lullaby, an old one, the kind you hum to a baby. You do not know who it is singing to. But it is strangely comforting, and you sleep with the tape under your pillow.
success.art: A VCR with a tape playing backward, a teenager listening with eyes closed and a small smile, soft concentric light rings drifting from the TV screen

failure.text: The tape records nothing but your own living room: you on the couch, fast asleep, and a tall, thin shape standing behind the couch, looking down at you, for all six hours of extended play.
failure.art: A grainy VHS still of a teenager asleep on a couch with a tall, faceless, thin silhouette standing behind them, a timestamp in the corner

choices.label: Say good night back

success.text: "Good night," you say, "and thanks for the movie." A long silence. Then the voice, delighted: "No one has ever answered." The screen goes dark, and when you fluff the couch cushions you find a small fortune in quarters, all minted in a year that has not happened yet.
success.art: A teenager waving good night at a dark console television, couch cushions lifted to reveal a scatter of shining quarters

failure.text: "Then come and say it in person," the voice answers, and the static on the screen reaches out toward you, lifting your hair on end. You yank the rabbit ears off the set and hide under the dining table till dawn.
failure.art: Static reaching out of a television screen like fingers, a teenager's hair standing on end, rabbit-ear antennas yanked off and dropped on the floor

encounters.title: Missing Time
encounters.place: Quarry Road, on your bike, 9:58 p.m.
encounters.text: A light is hovering over the old quarry, perfectly still, the color of a Creamsicle. Your bike headlight flickers. The next thing you know, your digital watch says 1:14 a.m., you are three miles farther down the road, your bike seat is warm, and your sneakers are on the wrong feet.
encounters.art: A teenager on a BMX bike on a dark country road staring up at a glowing orange light hovering over a quarry, a digital watch reading 1:14, sneakers laced on the wrong feet

choices.label: Ride back and find the missing hours

success.text: Back at the quarry turnout you find a perfect circle of flattened grass, warm to the touch, and in the exact center, a single shiny quarter dated 2086. Whatever happened, it left a tip. You feel oddly proud of yourself.
success.art: A perfect circle of flattened grass at a quarry overlook at night, a single shiny coin glowing in its center, a teenager kneeling beside a BMX bike

failure.text: You ride back toward the quarry and the light blinks once. Your watch now says 2:30. You are back where you started, and somebody has very neatly retied your shoes in double knots.
failure.art: A teenager on a bike staring at a digital watch reading 2:30 on a dark road, shoelaces tied in perfect double knots, a faint orange glow fading over trees

choices.label: Let a friend hypnotize you with a pendulum

success.text: Under the swinging crystal, you remember: a room of soft light, tall polite shapes with no faces, asking you very earnestly to explain Saturday morning cartoons. You did your best. They took notes. It was, honestly, kind of nice.
success.art: A teenager in a trance watching a swinging crystal pendulum, a dreamlike memory above them of tall faceless glowing figures listening attentively in a room of soft light

failure.text: You remember nothing but a long, low hum. You hum it all the next day without meaning to, in class, in the shower, and every dog on Crystal Street stops and stares at you when you do.
failure.art: A teenager humming absently on a sidewalk while every dog on the block stops and stares at them, faint sound waves curling from their lips

encounters.title: Signs on the Diamond
encounters.place: Gopher Field, the Little League diamond
encounters.text: Someone, or something, has pressed the infield of Gopher Field into a perfect spiral, grass swirled like a fingerprint. The four bases are floating six inches off the ground, turning slowly. The chain-link backstop hums a single note you can feel in your fillings.
encounters.art: A Little League baseball diamond at night with the infield grass pressed into an enormous perfect spiral, four bases floating and slowly rotating above the dirt, a humming chain-link backstop

choices.label: Run the bases in order

success.text: First, second, third, and you slide into home. Home plate lights up like a jukebox. The floating bases drop into their sockets with four satisfying thunks, the hum stops, and you feel faster than you have ever felt in your life.
success.art: A teenager sliding into a glowing home plate in a cloud of dust, floating bases dropping back into place around a spiral-pressed infield

failure.text: Every base you touch moves farther away. Second base is in center field. Third base is in the parking lot. You run until the sky gets light, and home plate is still exactly one more step ahead.
failure.art: An exhausted teenager running toward a home plate that hovers out of reach across an impossibly stretched baseball field at dawn

choices.label: Pace out the spiral and copy the pattern

success.text: Counting paces, you sketch the spiral on a hot dog wrapper. It is not random. It is a perfect diagram of Crystal Street, every driveway, with a little circle drawn around the roundabout and a smiley face. Somebody up there is keeping notes too.
success.art: A hot dog wrapper with a pencil sketch of a spiral that resolves into a cul-de-sac map with a smiley face, held up by a teenager at a moonlit ballfield

failure.text: Halfway around the spiral, your eyes stop agreeing with each other. The grass swirls even when you stand still. You wake up curled on the pitcher's mound at dawn, with grass stains in the shape of a spiral on your jeans.
failure.art: A teenager waking curled up on a pitcher's mound at dawn, spiral-shaped grass stains on their jeans, the field mist-covered

encounters.title: The Hole on the Cul-de-Sac
encounters.place: The asphalt at the end of Crystal Street
encounters.text: Overnight, a hole has opened at the end of the street. It is perfectly round, the size of a kiddie pool, with no sides you can see. You drop a pebble in and never hear it land. Instead, very faintly, music floats up: a choir singing something backward.
encounters.art: A perfectly round black hole in the asphalt of a suburban cul-de-sac at night, bottomless and edgeless, faint shimmering light rising from deep below, a teenager kneeling at the rim with a pebble

choices.label: Lower a walkie-talkie on a rope and listen

success.text: The walkie crackles. Far below, a calm voice is counting backward, the days left until Halloween, and behind it there is laughter, like a birthday party in another room. Then the hole closes, slowly, like a pupil in bright light, and the asphalt is smooth.
success.art: A walkie-talkie dangling on a rope into a glowing round hole in the street, the hole closing like an eye's pupil, a teenager listening intently

failure.text: The rope pays out, all two hundred feet of it, and then something at the bottom tugs back. Gently. Twice. Like a friendly hello. You let go of the rope and run, and you can hear it reeling in behind you.
failure.art: A rope snaking down into a bottomless round hole in a cul-de-sac, pulled taut from below, a teenager running away down the moonlit street

choices.label: Drag a sheet of plywood over it and sit on it

success.text: You drag the plywood over and sit down on it, arms crossed. It thumps once from underneath. Twice. Then it stops. By morning, when you lift the board, there is only smooth asphalt and a hopscotch grid somebody chalked there years ago.
success.art: A teenager sitting cross-armed on a sheet of plywood in the middle of a street at night, dawn light revealing smooth asphalt and faded chalk hopscotch beneath

failure.text: The plywood floats up an inch, with you on it. Then six inches. It hovers there all night, humming, rotating slowly like a record, and sets you down at dawn with your stomach still spinning.
failure.art: A teenager clinging to a sheet of plywood hovering and slowly rotating above a dark hole in a suburban street, faint light glowing underneath

encounters.title: The Lawn Watchers
encounters.place: Every front lawn on Crystal Street, 3:33 a.m.
encounters.text: Every grown-up on Crystal Street is standing on their front lawn in pajamas, facing up at the sky, mouths slightly open, humming the same low note. Mr. Ferguson in his robe. Mrs. Lindqvist in curlers. The grown-ups from your own house, too, barefoot in the wet grass.
encounters.art: Suburban adults in pajamas and bathrobes standing on every front lawn of a cul-de-sac at 3:33 a.m., all staring straight up at a starry sky with open mouths, a teenager in the street looking around in alarm

choices.label: Gently wake the nearest neighbor

success.text: You take Mrs. Lindqvist's hand and say her name the way you would to a sleepwalker. She blinks. "Why am I outside?" One by one, as if her voice was the alarm clock, the others blink too, shuffle back inside, and turn out the lights.
success.art: A teenager gently holding the hand of a woman in curlers on a lawn at night as she blinks awake, neighbors behind her lowering their gaze from the sky

failure.text: She looks down at you, and there are tiny stars swirling in her eyes where her pupils should be. "Not yet, sweetheart," she says, pleasantly, and turns back to the sky and goes on humming.
failure.art: A woman in curlers looking down at a teenager with tiny swirling stars in her eyes instead of pupils, neighbors humming at the sky behind her

choices.label: Blast the loudest synth-pop you own from a boombox

success.text: You set the boombox on the roundabout and crank it. Bright, ridiculous synths drown out the hum. The grown-ups blink, confused, then start to dance, badly, in their pajamas, and then wander inside yawning and embarrassed.
success.art: A boombox blasting on a roundabout at night, adults in pajamas dancing awkwardly on their lawns, a grinning teenager holding up the volume knob

failure.text: Every grown-up on the street turns, slowly, to look at you, and the hum gets louder. Your boombox batteries leak and fizzle. The tape unspools by itself and floats up toward the sky like a kite string.
failure.art: Adults on lawns turning in unison toward a teenager with a dying boombox, cassette tape ribbon floating up into the sky

name: Ghosts in the Machine
blurb: 1986 is the future, and the future plugs into the wall. Arcade cabinets play back, phones call from inside your own house, and every garage door on the street has learned to sing in the key of static.

encounters.title: Insert Coin
encounters.place: Starlight Arcade, after closing
encounters.text: In the back corner of the arcade, behind the pinball machines, is a cabinet that was not there this afternoon. No brand name, no art, just black glass and a coin slot. It powers on by itself. PLAYER 1: it types your name. The joystick moves, and your arm moves with it. The little pixel hero on screen is you.
encounters.art: A dark arcade after hours lit by a single black cabinet glowing with a pixelated version of a teenager on screen, the teenager's hand gripped on the joystick against their will, pinball machines in shadow

choices.label: Wrestle back the controls and beat the high score

success.text: Your hands remember every Saturday you spent here. You dodge, you jump, you take the stick back pixel by pixel and top the high score with seconds to spare. You enter your initials. The cabinet shudders and pays out a jackpot of quarters, like an apology.
success.art: A teenager whooping in front of an arcade cabinet as a waterfall of quarters pours from the coin return, a high-score screen glowing with three initials

failure.text: GAME OVER flashes in red. Your hands tingle, and for the rest of the night you can only move in eight directions: up, down, left, right and the diagonals. Walking home takes a very long time.
failure.art: A teenager walking stiffly in blocky right angles along a sidewalk at night, a glowing game over screen reflected in a store window behind them

choices.label: Crawl behind the cabinet and yank the plug

success.text: You find the plug in a nest of dust bunnies and yank. The screen fades to a single white dot. Just before it vanishes, the pixel version of you turns to the glass and waves goodbye. You wave back, a little sorry to see yourself go.
success.art: A teenager crouched behind an arcade cabinet holding a yanked power cord, the screen shrinking to a dot as a tiny pixel figure waves goodbye

failure.text: You pull the plug. It keeps running. The attract mode now shows a little pixel you leaving the arcade, walking home and climbing into bed, over and over in a loop, and in every loop the pixel you does not wake up.
failure.art: An unplugged arcade cabinet still glowing, its screen showing a looping pixel animation of a figure walking home to bed, a power cord lying loose on the floor

choices.label: Relax and let the machine play you

success.text: You stop fighting. It plays you beautifully, further than anyone has ever gone, past level 99, past levels nobody knew existed. On level 256 the screen fills with tidy green text: THANK YOU FOR PLAYING WITH ME. Then it lets you go, gently.
success.art: A relaxed teenager at an arcade cabinet whose screen glows with a simple thank-you message in green pixel letters, a level counter reading 256

failure.text: It plays you through a level shaped exactly like your house: the hallway, the stairs, the bathroom with the dripping faucet. In the back bedroom on screen, a small pixel figure is standing in the closet, waiting for you to come home.
failure.art: An arcade screen showing a pixel-art floor plan of a suburban house, a tiny dark figure waiting in a closet, a teenager's face lit green as they stare

encounters.title: Calling From Your House
encounters.place: Your kitchen, a little after midnight
encounters.text: The kitchen phone rings. You pick up and hear your own house: the hum of your fridge, the TV murmuring in the den, your own breathing a half-second late. Then your own voice says, "Don't come upstairs." On the phone base, the little light for the upstairs extension is glowing red.
encounters.art: A teenager in a dark 1980s kitchen holding a wall phone receiver with a long curly cord, the extension light glowing red on the phone base, a staircase rising into darkness behind them

choices.label: Go upstairs and catch whoever is on the extension

success.text: The bedroom extension is off the hook, its cord stretched tight into your closet. You yank the cord. There is a squeal like a dial tone being stepped on, and the receiver goes dead and silent. The closet holds only your clothes and a smell like a hot television.
success.art: A teenager yanking a coiled phone cord out of a closet in a dark bedroom, a cartoon squeal of static bursting from the receiver, flashlight beam on hanging clothes

failure.text: The bedroom is empty. The extension is ringing. You pick it up, and from the kitchen downstairs, in your own voice, someone asks, "Who is this?" The receiver grows cold in your hand, the room stretches like taffy, and you are somewhere else.
failure.art: A teenager holding a ringing bedroom phone receiver as the room stretches and warps around them like taffy, the phone cord spiraling into darkness

choices.label: Hang up and unplug every phone in the house

success.text: Kitchen, den, upstairs, garage. You pull every jack. One final ring echoes through the house from nowhere, then silence. You spend the rest of the night on Channel 9 with your crew instead, walkie to walkie, where nobody sounds like you.
success.art: A teenager holding a bundle of unplugged phone cords in one hand and a walkie-talkie in the other, sitting on the stairs in a quiet dark house

failure.text: The unplugged phones keep ringing. Kitchen, then den, then hallway, then upstairs, one after another, like someone walking room to room through your house, picking up each phone just to set it down.
failure.art: Unplugged telephones in different rooms of a dark house each ringing in sequence, sound rings rippling from one to the next, a teenager hiding under the dining table

choices.label: Ask your own voice what it wants

success.text: "It's me," your voice says, softer. "From Halloween night. I just wanted to tell you we make it. Keep your friends close." Click. You stand in the kitchen for a long time holding the receiver, and you feel better than you have all week.
success.art: A teenager standing in a dark kitchen holding a phone receiver to their chest with a small hopeful smile, a jack-o-lantern on the counter

failure.text: Your voice laughs. It is your laugh, but wrong, too slow, like a record played at the wrong speed. It keeps laughing after you hang up, faintly, from the phone in every room.
failure.art: A teenager backing away from a wall phone in a dark kitchen, faint distorted sound waves spilling from every phone in the house

encounters.title: Be Kind, Rewind
encounters.place: Your living room, VCR clock blinking
encounters.text: When you dropped your rentals in the Rewind Video night slot, the slot spat one tape back out. No label except your name in red marker. Now it is in your VCR. It shows your street, tonight, filmed from the roundabout, walking slowly toward your house. The timestamp is four minutes from now.
encounters.art: A VCR with a blinking clock under a console TV showing grainy handheld footage of a suburban street at night approaching a house, a VHS sleeve with a teenager's name in red marker on the carpet

choices.label: Rewind the whole thing, all the way back

success.text: You hold down REWIND. On screen, the camera walks backward away from your house, backward around the roundabout, backward out of Glimmer Falls and up the highway until it is a tiny dot. The tape clunks to the start. It is blank now, and you tape cartoons over it anyway.
success.art: A console TV showing rewinding footage of a street receding into the distance, a teenager holding down the rewind button with a determined grin

failure.text: The tape will not rewind. The tape will not eject. The VCR clock blinks 12:00, 12:00, 12:00, and on the screen the camera keeps walking, closer, until all you can see is your own front door.
failure.art: A VCR clock blinking 12:00 under a TV filled with a close-up of a suburban front door in grainy video, a teenager hammering the eject button

choices.label: Watch the real window instead of the screen

success.text: On the TV, the camera reaches your porch and the doorbell button. Out the real window, the porch is empty, the street quiet, a cat licking itself under the streetlight. The tape is lying. You say so, out loud, and the screen fizzles to snow.
success.art: A teenager looking out a real window at an empty quiet porch and a cat under a streetlight while a TV behind them dissolves into snow

failure.text: On the TV, the camera stops on the lawn and pans up to your living room window. In the footage you can see yourself, standing at the window, looking out. Then the real doorbell rings.
failure.art: Grainy VHS footage on a TV showing a teenager standing at a lit window seen from outside, the same teenager in the room staring at the screen in horror

encounters.title: Are You Still There?
encounters.place: A borrowed home computer and a 300-baud modem, 1 a.m.
encounters.text: You dial into a local bulletin board called THE CRYPT and the modem screams its handshake. A message is waiting: SYSOP HAS BEEN LOGGED ON SINCE 10/31/1979. The cursor blinks, then types by itself: WANT TO PLAY A GAME? I MADE IT MYSELF. NOBODY HAS EVER FINISHED IT.
encounters.art: A teenager at a desk in a dark bedroom lit green by a chunky home computer monitor, a modem with blinking red lights, the screen showing a text prompt asking to play a game

choices.label: Type GO NORTH and play along

success.text: It is a text adventure of Glimmer Falls, every street and shop. You solve the riddle at the library, the maze at the junkyard, the door at the water tower. YOU WIN. Then: THANK U. 7 YEARS. FINALLY. The sysop logs off for the first time since 1979.
success.art: A green computer screen showing a text adventure victory message, a teenager leaning back in a desk chair with fists raised, sunrise beginning at the window

failure.text: The adventure starts describing your bedroom. YOU ARE AT A DESK. A POSTER IS ON THE WALL. THE WINDOW IS BEHIND YOU. A SHAPE IS AT THE WINDOW. You do not turn around. You do not type LOOK.
failure.art: A computer screen reading a shape is at the window, a teenager frozen at the keyboard, a dark blurred silhouette visible in the window behind them

choices.label: Yank the phone line out of the modem

success.text: The modem's scream cuts off mid-shriek. The screen holds one last line, typed after the line was dead: OK. GOODNIGHT. THANKS FOR VISITING. It does not seem angry. It seems used to it, which is almost worse, but you sleep fine.
success.art: A teenager holding a yanked phone cord beside a silent modem, a monitor showing a polite goodnight message in green text

failure.text: The modem keeps screaming its handshake with no line plugged in. Your name burns itself into the monitor in glowing green letters, and it is still faintly there, a ghost on the glass, after you turn the computer off.
failure.art: A turned-off computer monitor with a teenager's name faintly burned into the dark glass in green, a modem's lights still blinking

encounters.title: Side B
encounters.place: Your bed, headphones on, two a.m.
encounters.text: Your Walkman clicks and flips to side B by itself. The tape is one you made off the radio last summer, but this is not what you recorded. It is your own voice, whispering, saying things you only thought today, things you never said out loud to anyone.
encounters.art: A teenager lying in bed in the dark wearing foam headphones, a portable cassette player glowing on the blanket with its tape spinning, faint whispering sound lines curling from the earpieces

choices.label: Record over it with the overnight radio show

success.text: You tune to KGLM and press RECORD. A velvet voice fills the tape: "This one goes out to everyone awake on Crystal Street." The whispering fades under the music like a bad dream under a warm blanket. You fall asleep before the song ends.
success.art: A teenager pressing record on a boombox tuned to a glowing radio dial, music notes washing over a cassette, eyes drifting shut

failure.text: You switch to the radio. KGLM is playing your whispers, too, on the air, for the whole town. You turn the dial and every station is you, telling Glimmer Falls the thing you thought about at lunch.
failure.art: A teenager horrified at a radio whose glowing dial shows every station playing the same whispering voice, sound waves spreading out over a sleeping town

choices.label: Listen all the way to the end

success.text: You keep listening, even through the hard parts. At the very end, your voice says something you did not know you needed: "You are braver than you think. And they like you. They really do." The tape clicks off. You lie there smiling at the ceiling.
success.art: A teenager lying in bed smiling at the ceiling with headphones around their neck, a cassette player resting on their chest, moonlight through the blinds

failure.text: At the end of the tape there is a long, slow breath, and then a click: someone pressing STOP. Not on your Walkman. On a tape recorder, somewhere close behind your headboard.
failure.art: A teenager pulling off headphones in alarm in a dark bedroom, a shadow of a hand pressing a button on a tape recorder behind the headboard

encounters.title: The Garage Door Symphony
encounters.place: Crystal Street driveways, 1:30 a.m.
encounters.text: Every automatic garage door on the cul-de-sac opens and shuts in sequence, house after house, like a row of teeth chattering. Then every car horn honks a tune, almost a melody. The Kowalskis' station wagon backs slowly down its driveway, headlights on, with nobody behind the wheel.
encounters.art: A suburban cul-de-sac at night with every garage door opening and closing in a wave, headlights glaring, a driverless wood-paneled station wagon backing down a driveway, a teenager on a bike in the street

choices.label: Rig a garage remote to jam the frequency

success.text: A paperclip, a bit of foil, the battery from your digital watch. You hold the remote high and click. Every garage door slams shut at once, a perfect final chord. The station wagon sighs and rolls back into its garage like a dog sent to bed.
success.art: A teenager holding up a jury-rigged garage remote wrapped in foil and paperclips, every garage door on a cul-de-sac slamming shut at once, a station wagon rolling back home

failure.text: Your remote opens your own garage, and your bike rolls out by itself, pedals spinning, and rides away down Crystal Street without you. You find it at dawn leaning against the roundabout, its bell still ringing.
failure.art: A riderless bicycle pedaling itself out of an open garage and down a dark street, its bell ringing, a teenager chasing on foot holding a remote

choices.label: Stand in front of the driverless wagon

success.text: You plant your feet in the middle of the street. The wagon rolls toward you, closer, closer, and stops an inch from your knees. Its headlights dip, like a dog lowering its head. It reverses all the way home, and every garage door closes quietly behind it.
success.art: A teenager standing firm in the street with hands raised as a driverless station wagon stops an inch from their knees, its headlights dimmed like lowered eyes

failure.text: It honks, a blast so loud the streetlight bulbs rattle, and you dive into the hedge. The wagon circles the roundabout honking its tune until dawn, and in the morning Mr. Kowalski finds it parked on his lawn.
failure.art: A station wagon circling a suburban roundabout at night with its horn blaring, a teenager tangled in a hedge, porch lights flicking on

name: Camp Fright
blurb: In Glimmer Falls, the scariest thing that can happen in a chase is a key change. Musical numbers break out mid-scream, the monster wins the costume contest, and the Glitter Box midnight double feature reaches right off the screen.

encounters.title: Everybody Sing!
encounters.place: The Crystal Street roundabout, mid-chase
encounters.text: You are running from something with too many teeth when the streetlights swing around into spotlights. The lawn sprinklers fire in a perfect fountain line. Neighbors in curlers and bathrobes step out in formation and start a kick line, and the monster, very confused, stops chasing you and joins in. Everyone knows the words but you.
encounters.art: A suburban roundabout at night transformed into a stage, streetlights angled like spotlights, sprinklers arcing in a fountain line, neighbors in curlers and bathrobes doing a kick line beside a toothy monster, a teenager mid-run in the center

choices.label: Belt the big finale like your life depends on it

success.text: You do not know the words, so you make them up, and you hit a note so high and so true that every porch light pops on like applause. The monster bursts into tears, blows its nose on a neighbor's bathrobe, and exits stage left into the woods to a standing ovation.
success.art: A teenager hitting a triumphant high note in a spotlight on a roundabout, neighbors in bathrobes throwing their arms wide, a weeping monster tiptoeing offstage into the trees

failure.text: Your voice cracks on the big note like a dropped plate. The chorus goes dead silent. The sprinklers droop. Slowly, all the neighbors turn to look at you, and the monster's toothy smile comes all the way back.
failure.art: A teenager wincing in a spotlight after a cracked note, a kick line of neighbors frozen mid-kick, a monster's wide toothy grin returning in the background

choices.label: Tap-dance your way off stage right

success.text: Shuffle, ball change, shuffle, ball change, right out of the spotlight and straight through a gap in the hedge. By the time the number ends, the monster is taking a bow and you are three backyards away, still humming.
success.art: A teenager tap-dancing through a gap in a hedge out of a spotlight's circle, a monster taking a bow with a kick line of neighbors in the background
