failure.text: You trip over a sprinkler head mid-step. The monster catches you, dips you low like a tango partner, and grins down at you with breath like a bag of old Halloween candy. Then the music ends, and it drops you in the azaleas.
failure.art: A grinning monster dipping a startled teenager like a tango partner in a spotlight, neighbors in curlers watching, azalea bushes waiting below

choices.label: Take over as choreographer and steer the kick line

success.text: "Five, six, seven, eight!" You march the kick line into a wall between you and the monster, then turn it into a conga that dances the monster right out of the cul-de-sac and down Quarry Road. Mrs. Lindqvist says it is the best number the street has ever done.
success.art: A teenager directing a conga line of neighbors in bathrobes that escorts a bewildered monster down a suburban street under spotlights

failure.text: Your blocking is a disaster. Half the line kicks left, half kicks right, and somebody's slipper hits you square in the chest. You land in the roundabout garden while the monster takes your mark.
failure.art: A chaotic kick line colliding in every direction, a fuzzy slipper flying through the air, a teenager toppling into a garden bed

encounters.title: And the Winner Is
encounters.place: Center court of the Starlight Mall, the late-night costume contest
encounters.text: The mall's Halloween costume contest is down to two finalists: you, and a ten-foot oozing thing with antlers and three rows of teeth that everyone agrees is the most realistic costume they have ever seen. The judges hand it the trophy. It takes the trophy. Then it picks up the nearest judge.
encounters.art: A neon-lit mall center court with a costume contest stage, a ten-foot oozing antlered monster holding a trophy in one claw and a startled judge in the other, a teenager in a homemade costume beside it, a crowd cheering

choices.label: Demand a recount, loudly, with procedure

success.text: "Point of order! Rule four: costumes must be removable!" The judges confer. The monster is disqualified. It puts the judge down, sulks, accepts an honorable mention ribbon and slinks out through the food court. You win runner-up and the cash prize.
success.art: A teenager pointing at a rulebook on a mall stage while judges confer, a sulking ten-foot monster wearing an honorable mention ribbon slinking toward the food court

failure.text: The crowd votes again. The monster wins by an even bigger margin. It pats you on the head with a slimy, sympathetic claw, the way a grown-up pats a kid who tried their best, and carries the judge off into the dead wing.
failure.art: A ten-foot slimy monster patting a deflated teenager on the head on a mall stage, a cheering crowd, a judge tucked under its arm

choices.label: Try to find the zipper

success.text: There is no zipper, but there is a very ticklish spot just under the third row of teeth. The monster shrieks with laughter, drops the judge, drops the trophy, and flees through the fountain, giggling all the way to the parking lot.
success.art: A teenager tickling a giant oozing monster under its jaw, the monster doubled over laughing, a judge tumbling free onto a mall stage

failure.text: There is no zipper. There is, however, a mouth exactly where a zipper would be, and it says, politely, "Do you mind?" You run all the way home in your costume.
failure.art: A teenager recoiling from a mouth opening in the belly of a towering costume-contest monster on a mall stage

encounters.title: Midnight at the Glitter Box
encounters.place: The Glitter Box Playhouse, Saturday midnight double feature
encounters.text: The Glitter Box is packed for the midnight double feature: "The Martian Bride of Dr. Glamour" followed by a cheap slasher nobody stays for. The audience is in lab coats and fishnets, throwing toast and shouting every callback. When the whole house gets up for the big dance number, the Moon Hop, the screen ripples like water, and the front row starts sliding into it.
encounters.art: A glittering old movie palace at midnight packed with a costumed audience in lab coats and sequins dancing in the aisles, toast flying, the movie screen rippling like water as the front row slides into it

choices.label: Do the Moon Hop with the whole house

success.text: A hop to the left, a shimmy to the right, and three hundred people hit every step in perfect sync. The screen burps the front row back into their seats, covered in glitter and grinning. On screen, Dr. Glamour blows the audience a kiss. Frankie tosses you a glow bracelet from the booth.
success.art: A whole theater audience in lab coats and fishnets doing a synchronized dance in the aisles, the front row tumbling back out of a movie screen in a burst of glitter

failure.text: You hop left when everyone else hops right, and the screen reaches out and takes you instead. You tumble through the silver light, past Dr. Glamour's laboratory, and out the other side into the second feature, the cheap slasher that nobody stays for.
failure.art: A teenager tumbling headfirst into a rippling silver movie screen while a costumed audience reaches after them, the next film's dark title card glimpsed inside

choices.label: Shout the callbacks louder than the film

success.text: You know every line, and you hit every one. The film's villain, a man in a silver cape, actually cracks up on screen and breaks character. The rippling stops. The audience roars. The movie, a little sheepish, goes back to being a movie.
success.art: A teenager standing on a theater seat shouting at a movie screen where a caped villain doubles over laughing, the audience cheering and throwing toast

failure.text: You shout the wrong line, at the wrong time. The whole movie stops. Every actor on screen turns, slowly, and looks at you, and the projector beam swings off the screen and pins you in your seat like a spotlight.
failure.art: Every actor on a movie screen turned to stare out at the audience, a projector beam pinning one teenager in their theater seat

choices.label: Climb to the projection booth and splice in a cartoon

success.text: You find a cartoon reel in a can marked EMERGENCY, thread it, and splice. The screen flickers to a rabbit playing a piano. Whatever was reaching out of the movie gets distracted and starts tapping its foot. The crowd cheers the intermission, and someone tips you a quarter.
success.art: A teenager splicing film in a cramped projection booth full of reels, a cartoon playing on the distant screen below, the audience cheering

failure.text: The reel unspools in your hands and keeps going, looping around you, faster and faster, until you are wrapped up like a mummy in thirty-five millimeter film. Frankie finds you there after the show and cuts you out with nail scissors.
failure.art: A teenager wrapped head to toe in loops of movie film like a mummy in a projection booth, a stage manager with a headset arriving with tiny scissors

encounters.title: The Cheapest Haunted Hayride in California
encounters.place: The Jaycees Haunted Hayride, Quarry Road
encounters.text: The Jaycees hayride has always been terrible: rubber bats on fishing line, plywood tombstones, a dad in a sheet. Tonight it has all come alive, and it is still terrible. The bats squeak. The rubber werewolf's mask slips. The plywood tombstones are chasing the wagon, falling over every ten feet and getting back up.
encounters.art: A hay wagon full of teens rolling down a dark country road chased by plywood tombstones, rubber bats bouncing on fishing line, a man in a bedsheet ghost costume floating above the hay, a rubber werewolf with a slipping mask

choices.label: Give the monsters notes on their performance

success.text: "Darling, where is your motivation? Why are you haunting?" The monsters stop, huddle, and rehearse. They give one genuinely terrifying encore, and you all scream, and then they bow and go back to being props. Even the sheet waves goodbye.
success.art: A teenager standing on a hay wagon directing a huddle of cheap rubber monsters and plywood tombstones like a movie director, the monsters taking a bow afterward

failure.text: They take your notes very seriously. They come back scarier, much scarier, with better lighting and a fog machine from somewhere. The werewolf's mask is not slipping anymore. It never was a mask.
failure.art: A suddenly terrifying hayride with rolling fog and eerie lighting, a real bare-faced werewolf lunging from the trees at a hay wagon full of screaming teens

choices.label: Jump off the wagon and run for the road

success.text: You leap, roll through the hay, and sprint. A papier-mache ghoul chases you as far as the road, huffing, and then gives up and sits on a fence post to catch its breath. You wave. It waves back, a little embarrassed.
success.art: A teenager sprinting onto a moonlit road with hay in their hair, a papier-mache ghoul slumped on a fence post behind them catching its breath

failure.text: You land in the fake swamp next to the trail. It is not fake anymore. It is cold, it is deep, and it smells like a hundred years of frogs. You climb out with a rubber bat stuck in your hair, and it squeaks in your ear all the way home.
failure.art: A teenager climbing out of a muddy swamp beside a hayride trail at night with a rubber bat tangled in their hair, a hay wagon rolling away

encounters.title: The Show Must Go On
encounters.place: The Glitter Box Playhouse, the late drag revue
encounters.text: Glory is mid-number, sequins blazing, when the stage trapdoor creaks open and something slick and many-armed climbs into the spotlight. The audience roars. They think it is part of the act. In the wings, Frankie presses her headset and hisses, "That is NOT on the cue sheet."
encounters.art: A glittering cabaret stage under hot spotlights, a drag queen in blazing sequins mid-pose as a slick many-armed creature climbs out of a trapdoor beside her, the audience cheering, a stage manager in a headset in the wings

choices.label: Jump on stage and make it part of the act

success.text: You and Glory each grab an arm, or a tentacle, and twirl it into a three-way duet. It turns pink. It is blushing. At the bow it waves all eight arms and sinks back down the trapdoor to a standing ovation. The tip jar is overflowing, and Glory splits it with you.
success.art: A teenager and a drag queen twirling a blushing pink tentacled creature across a glittering stage, the audience on its feet, a tip jar overflowing

failure.text: You freeze in the spotlight. The creature wraps you in a feather boa and starts dragging you toward the trapdoor while the audience cheers even louder. Frankie hauls on a sandbag rope and the curtain drops on both of you, just in time.
failure.art: A frozen teenager being wrapped in a feather boa by a tentacled creature and dragged toward a stage trapdoor, a curtain crashing down

choices.label: Run the light board and blind it

success.text: Frankie points at a fader. You slam it. Strobes fire, the mirror ball blazes, and the creature covers all its eyes at once and dives back down the trapdoor. The audience thinks it was the best special effect the Glitter Box has ever done.
success.art: A teenager slamming a fader on a lighting board as strobe lights blaze across a stage, a tentacled creature diving into a trapdoor with arms over its eyes

failure.text: Wrong fader. Total blackout. The audience screams with delight. In the dark, something wet and cool slides gently over your sneakers on its way past, and when the lights come back up, the creature is gone and so is Glory's best wig.
failure.art: A pitch-dark theater lit only by exit signs, a glistening trail across the stage floor, an empty wig stand, a teenager frozen at a lighting board

encounters.title: The Container Party
encounters.place: Mrs. Feeney's living room, a late-night Seal-a-Fresh party
encounters.text: Mrs. Feeney's Seal-a-Fresh party has run very late. The pastel plastic containers on the coffee table have started burping back when you burp their lids. Then they start snapping. The hostess keeps smiling, keeps passing around the catalog, as a stack of lidded bowls hops off the table and hunts for ankles.
encounters.art: A pastel 1980s suburban living room at a home sales party, plastic food containers snapping their lids and hopping across a coffee table, a smiling hostess holding a catalog, guests lifting their feet onto the sofa

choices.label: Burp every lid at once to seal them shut

success.text: You line them up and press every lid in one long, glorious FWOOMP. The containers seal tight with whatever was inside them trapped for good. Mrs. Feeney is so impressed she gives you the hostess gift, which you sell back to her for quarters.
success.art: A teenager pressing down a whole row of pastel plastic container lids at once with a giant puff of air, guests applauding from the sofa

failure.text: One lid bites down on your finger and will not let go. The rest of the stack chases you around the coffee table three times while the guests politely lift their feet and Mrs. Feeney explains the lifetime warranty.
failure.art: A teenager running around a coffee table with a plastic container clamped on one finger, a stack of snapping containers in pursuit, a hostess smiling serenely

choices.label: Out-sell the hostess at her own party

success.text: You grab the catalog and give the pitch of your life. The guests order everything. Even the possessed containers are so moved by your pitch that they file into their shipping box in an orderly line, ready to be mailed somewhere very far away.
success.art: A teenager giving a dramatic sales pitch holding a pastel bowl aloft, plastic containers marching in a line into a cardboard shipping box, guests waving order forms

failure.text: Somehow, by the end of your pitch, you have bought forty dollars of plastic you cannot afford. The order includes a lidded casserole dish that follows you home, hopping, and sleeps at the foot of your bed.
failure.art: A teenager walking home at night carrying an armload of plastic containers, a lidded casserole dish hopping along behind them like a puppy

name: The Neighborhood Fellowship
blurb: Somebody on Crystal Street has been ordering matching robes in bulk. Hooded bake sales, chain letters that sign your name for you, and a neighborhood watch meeting with a very unusual item four on the agenda.

encounters.title: The Hooded Bake Sale
encounters.place: A card table by the roundabout, midnight
encounters.text: There is a folding card table at the roundabout, covered in pies, brownies and lemon bars, with a hand-lettered sign: FELLOWSHIP BAKE SALE. It is staffed by neighbors in matching purple hooded robes and quilted oven mitts. "Everything's a quarter, dear," says a voice from inside a hood. "Eat it here." The lemon bars are humming.
encounters.art: A folding card table at a suburban roundabout at midnight piled with pies and brownies, neighbors in matching purple hooded robes and quilted oven mitts standing behind it, candles flickering, lemon bars glowing faintly

choices.label: Buy a brownie and see what happens

success.text: It is just a really good brownie. But for a second after you swallow, you can hear what everyone at the table is thinking: they are bored, and lonely, and nobody has asked them over in years. One of them lowers her hood. "Would you like the recipe?" she asks, and means it.
success.art: A teenager biting a brownie at a midnight bake sale while a woman in a purple robe lowers her hood and smiles shyly, recipe card in her oven mitt

failure.text: The brownie makes you feel enormously agreeable. You nod along to the chanting for an hour, then two. You wake up at dawn in a lawn chair beside the empty card table, with frosting on your face and a purple robe folded neatly in your lap.
failure.art: A teenager asleep in a lawn chair beside an empty card table at dawn, frosting on their cheek, a folded purple robe in their lap

choices.label: Swap their cash box for a coffee can of rock salt

success.text: At the stroke of one they open the cash box for the ritual, and rock salt sprays everywhere. The robes deflate like fallen souffles. Underneath are just your neighbors, blinking, embarrassed, in their pajamas. Somebody presses a whole pie into your hands to keep this quiet.
success.art: Rock salt spraying from an opened cash box at a midnight bake sale, purple robes collapsing to reveal embarrassed neighbors in pajamas, a teenager holding a pie

failure.text: They catch you. Nobody yells. They all just smile, warmly, and hand you a pie with your name piped across it in frosting, and a date underneath: OCT 31. "For later," someone says.
failure.art: Hooded neighbors smiling warmly as they hand a frightened teenager a pie with frosting lettering and a date piped on top

encounters.title: Send This to Thirteen Friends
encounters.place: Your mailbox, 12:01 a.m.
encounters.text: There is a letter in your mailbox in purple ink: THIS LETTER HAS BEEN AROUND THE WORLD NINE TIMES. COPY IT THIRTEEN TIMES BY HALLOWEEN OR THE FELLOWSHIP WILL COME FOR WHAT IS OWED. Below are signatures from every family on Crystal Street. The last line is your name, in your handwriting, and the ink is still wet.
encounters.art: A teenager at a suburban mailbox at midnight holding a letter written in glowing purple ink, a long column of signatures running down the page, the last one still wet

choices.label: Copy it thirteen times, but change one word in each

success.text: COME becomes CALL. OWED becomes OKAY. By the thirteenth copy the curse says THE FELLOWSHIP WILL CALL TO SEE IF YOU ARE OKAY. You mail them all. The next morning, three neighbors you have never talked to wave at you on your way to school.
success.art: A desk covered in thirteen handwritten letters with words crossed out and replaced, the last one reading a kind message, a teenager grinning with a purple pen

failure.text: Your pen keeps writing after you stop, adding names to the bottom of every copy: friends, teachers, your family. You drop it and it rolls across the desk, still scribbling, until it runs dry.
failure.art: A pen writing by itself across a stack of chain letters on a dark desk, adding a growing column of names, a teenager backing away

choices.label: Burn it in the backyard grill

success.text: The letter catches with a purple flame and a long, tired sigh, like someone setting down something heavy. The ash floats up and, for a second, spells THANKS in the air before the wind takes it. The grill smells faintly of lilacs all week.
success.art: A chain letter burning with purple flames in a kettle grill at night, its ash rising into the air in the shape of a word, a teenager watching with a lighter

failure.text: The letter will not burn. The flames slide right off it. In the morning there are thirteen copies of it in your mailbox, each one in your handwriting, and each one says you are running out of time.
failure.art: A suburban mailbox stuffed with thirteen identical purple-ink letters at dawn, an unburnt letter sitting in a cold grill nearby

choices.label: Follow the postmarks back to the first sender

success.text: The postmarks lead to a P.O. box at the old post office, closed since 1972. Inside are a thousand chain letters nobody ever mailed, and one apology from a lonely woman who just wanted people to write back. You write back. The letters stop coming.
success.art: A teenager opening a dusty post office box crammed with old letters, a single handwritten apology on top, flashlight light in an abandoned post office

failure.text: You follow the postmarks across town and back. Every trail ends at the same return address. It is your address. It has always been your address.
failure.art: A teenager staring at a stack of envelopes all postmarked with their own house address, standing on their own front walk at night

encounters.title: Neighborhood Watch Minutes
encounters.place: The Crystal Street homeowners' clubhouse, 11 p.m.
encounters.text: Folding chairs, a coffee urn, a podium, and every grown-up on the street wearing a hooded robe over a cardigan. The secretary reads the minutes. Item four on the agenda: SELECTING THIS YEAR'S OFFERING. Ballots are passed out. The nominees are whoever has the messiest lawn, and somebody has written your family's name in first.
encounters.art: A suburban clubhouse meeting room with folding chairs, a coffee urn and a podium, adults in hooded robes over cardigans passing out paper ballots, an agenda on an easel, a teenager peeking in from the doorway

choices.label: Call a point of order and filibuster

success.text: You read the bylaws aloud, all of them, including the parking rules. At 1:01 a.m. you reach Article Nine: no vote may be held after one in the morning. The chair bangs the gavel, furious and helpless. Meeting adjourned. Everyone shuffles home grumbling.
success.art: A teenager reading from a thick binder at a podium, a clock past one a.m. on the wall, robed adults slumped in folding chairs, a gavel coming down

failure.text: They vote to table your point of order. Then they vote to table you. You wake up at dawn wrapped in Christmas lights and taped to the clubhouse snack table, next to a plate of untouched deviled eggs.
failure.art: A teenager wrapped in Christmas lights and taped to a clubhouse snack table at dawn beside a plate of deviled eggs, folding chairs stacked around

choices.label: Nominate the homeowners' association president instead

success.text: "I nominate the president, for her service." The room erupts. Old grudges about fence heights and holiday lights pour out. Robes come off. Someone throws the coffee urn. You slip out the back while the Fellowship tears itself apart over a hedge dispute from 1974.
success.art: A suburban clubhouse meeting erupting into chaos, robed adults arguing and waving ballots, a coffee urn flying, a teenager slipping out a back door

failure.text: The vote is unanimous, but not for the president. Everyone writes in your name. They applaud, politely, and turn to look at you all at once, smiling. You run, and they do not follow. They do not need to.
failure.art: A room of robed adults applauding politely and turning to smile at a teenager by the door, a chalkboard tally showing one name

choices.label: Stuff the ballot box with write-ins for Nobody

success.text: Nobody wins, forty-seven votes to three. The secretary reads the result twice, confused. The ritual cannot proceed without an offering, and none of them is willing to be Nobody. They fold up the chairs and go home, deflated.
success.art: A secretary in a robe reading a ballot in confusion, a tally board showing an empty-chair landslide, a teenager hiding a fistful of ballots behind their back

failure.text: The secretary unfolds the ballots and reads out the results: your name, forty-seven times, in your handwriting. You know you wrote Nobody. Everyone turns to look at you, and the coffee urn begins to bubble.
failure.art: A robed secretary reading ballots aloud at a podium, every ballot showing the same name, a teenager pale in a folding chair, a coffee urn bubbling

encounters.title: The Welcome Wagon
encounters.place: Your front door, 12:30 a.m.
encounters.text: The doorbell rings after midnight. Three neighbors in identical pastel cardigans stand on your porch holding a foil-covered casserole. "Welcome to the neighborhood!" they say together. You have lived here your whole life. "We're so glad you're finally joining us." The foil on the casserole lifts, just a little, by itself.
encounters.art: Three smiling neighbors in identical pastel cardigans on a porch at night holding a foil-covered casserole dish whose foil is lifting by itself, a teenager peering out from a half-open front door

choices.label: Thank them warmly and shut the door

success.text: "That's so thoughtful. Good night!" You close the door gently but firmly. Through the peephole you watch their smiles flicker, uncertain, and then they leave. The casserole on the step is just tuna noodle, and it is honestly delicious.
success.art: A peephole view of three neighbors in cardigans walking away from a porch at night, a casserole dish left on the doormat

failure.text: One of them wedges a sensible loafer in the door before it closes. "That's all right," she says, still smiling. "We'll come back tomorrow. And the night after. And the night after that."
failure.art: A sensible loafer wedged in a closing front door, a smiling woman in a pastel cardigan peering through the gap

choices.label: Lift the foil and look inside

success.text: In the noodles is a tiny, furious, shrieking face. You grab the garden hose and blast it. The face dissolves, and so do the smiles: the three neighbors blink, look at their cardigans, and wander home in confused silence. One of them says she does not even like casseroles.
success.art: A teenager blasting a casserole dish with a garden hose, a tiny shrieking face dissolving in the noodles, three neighbors blinking in confusion on the porch

failure.text: Inside the casserole is a perfect little diorama of your house, built out of noodles. In the upstairs window is a tiny noodle figure of you. As you watch, the noodle front door slowly opens.
failure.art: A casserole dish containing a detailed miniature house built of noodles, a tiny noodle figure in an upstairs window, its front door opening

encounters.title: The Candle Walk
encounters.place: The roundabout, two a.m.
encounters.text: A ring of hooded figures with purple candles is circling the roundabout, chanting in what sounds like Latin. Listening closer, you realize it is the Glimmer Falls High fight song, backward. They are drawing a chalk circle on the asphalt as they walk, and there is exactly one empty spot left in the ring.
encounters.art: A ring of hooded figures holding purple candles circling a suburban roundabout at night, a chalk circle drawn on the asphalt, one gap in the ring, a teenager watching from behind a parked car

choices.label: Join the ring and chant something better

success.text: You step into the gap and chant a real blessing, the one for safe travel, the one grandmothers say. The candles turn from purple to warm gold. One by one the hoods fall back, and your neighbors look around, wondering why they are outside in their slippers.
success.art: A teenager chanting in a ring of hooded figures as the candles shift from purple to warm gold, hoods falling back to reveal confused neighbors in slippers

failure.text: You step in to change the chant, and your voice joins theirs perfectly, backward fight song and all, without you deciding to. You circle the roundabout with them until the candles burn out, and you know all the words now.
failure.art: A teenager walking in a ring of hooded chanting figures with a purple candle, eyes glazed, the chalk circle complete beneath their feet

choices.label: Smudge the chalk circle with your sneaker

success.text: One quick scuff while their backs are turned. The candles gutter all at once. The hooded figures stop, look at each other, mumble something about early mornings, and drift home in pairs. One of them leaves a perfectly good candle behind.
success.art: A sneaker scuffing a chalk circle on asphalt, purple candles guttering, hooded figures drifting away in pairs into the dark

failure.text: The chalk is wet paint. Your sneaker sticks fast. The ring turns inward and circles you, three times, slowly, candles held close to your face, and then leaves you there stuck to the street until the sun comes up.
failure.art: A teenager with one sneaker stuck to a painted circle on the street as hooded figures with candles circle tightly around them

encounters.title: A Golden Opportunity
encounters.place: A living room on Quarry Road, a late business opportunity night
encounters.text: A friend's aunt invited you to a Golden Tomorrow business opportunity night with free pizza. Everyone wears a little gold pin and the same enormous smile. On the easel is a pyramid chart of names, and the name at the very top has been scratched out so hard it tore the paper. "Who wants to change their life tonight?" the presenter asks.
encounters.art: A suburban living room at night full of smiling adults in gold lapel pins seated on folding chairs, a presenter beside an easel with a pyramid chart of names, the top name scratched out, pizza boxes on a side table

choices.label: Ask where the money actually goes

success.text: You go to the easel and do the math. By Thursday the pyramid needs four billion recruits. The room goes quiet. Gold pins start dropping onto the carpet like hail, and the guests leave in a hurry, taking the free pizza with them.
success.art: A teenager scribbling enormous math on an easel pad while gold pins fall from guests' lapels onto the carpet, the presenter's smile frozen

failure.text: "Great question!" beams the presenter. "That is what the top of the pyramid is for." Everyone turns to the chart. The scratched-out name at the top has been rewritten, neatly, in gold marker. It is yours.
failure.art: A pyramid chart on an easel with a teenager's name freshly written at the top in gold marker, a room full of smiling adults turning toward them

choices.label: Grab a slice and slip out through the kitchen

success.text: You leave with two slices, a free sample and a mint. Out on the sidewalk you glance back: every window of the house is shaped like a smile, and every smile is watching the street for someone else. You find a quarter on the walk and keep it.
success.art: A teenager walking away down a night sidewalk eating pizza, a suburban house behind them with every window curved into a smile

failure.text: Every exit has a smiling greeter with a clipboard. The back door, the garage, the bathroom window. By the time you get out, you have signed up for three months of Golden Tomorrow Sunshine Drops, and the first bill is already in your pocket.
failure.art: A teenager cornered at a back door by a smiling greeter holding a clipboard and pen, gold pins glinting, a kitchen full of smiling faces behind

name: Night Terrors
blurb: Close your eyes on Crystal Street this week and the rules go soft. You sleepwalk across the rooftops, your house grows an extra room, and the drained quarry lake comes back to fill the street, as deep as a held breath.

encounters.title: Sleepwalking the Rooftops
encounters.place: The roofs of Crystal Street, in your sleep
encounters.text: You wake, sort of, barefoot on your own roof in your pajamas, walking the ridge line with your arms out like a tightrope walker. The gutters glitter with frost. The roofs keep going, one after another, past the Lindqvists' chimney and on and on, past where the street should end.
encounters.art: A barefoot teenager in pajamas sleepwalking along the ridge line of a suburban rooftop at night with arms outstretched, frosty gutters glittering, an endless row of rooftops stretching toward a water tower under the stars

choices.label: Keep walking and trust your sleeping feet

success.text: You walk roof to roof as easily as crossing your bedroom, up the ladder of the KGLM water tower, and onto the catwalk at the very top. The stars are close enough to touch. You reach out, and one of them reaches back, and pulls you up into the sky.
success.art: A sleepwalking teenager in pajamas reaching up from the top of a water tower toward stars that are close enough to touch, one star reaching back like a hand

failure.text: A loose shingle slides under your heel and you slide with it, all the way to the gutter, and hang there by your fingertips. A neighbor's dog sees you and barks until the whole house wakes up and your folks fetch the ladder.
failure.art: A teenager in pajamas hanging from a rooftop gutter by their fingertips at night, a dog barking below, house lights coming on

choices.label: Count backward from ten and wake up gently

success.text: Ten, nine, eight. The endless roofs fold back into one. Three, two, one. You open your eyes sitting safely on your own roof, knees hugged to your chest, watching a cold, pink sunrise come up over the foothills. You climb back in the window and sleep until noon.
success.art: A teenager sitting safely on their own roof hugging their knees at sunrise, pink light over the foothills, an open bedroom window beside them

failure.text: You wake up halfway, which is the worst way. Suddenly the roof is very real and very high and very cold. You hug the chimney until the sky goes gray, too scared to move and too awake to go back to dreaming.
failure.art: A frightened teenager in pajamas clinging to a brick chimney on a steep roof in the gray before dawn

choices.label: Follow the black cat walking beside you

success.text: The cat walks with you, tail high, and leads you down a rose trellis, through your own open window and into bed. It curls up on your feet. In the morning there is no cat, but there is a single black whisker on your pillow.
success.art: A sleepwalking teenager following a black cat down a rose trellis toward an open bedroom window under a full moon

failure.text: The cat leads you through an open attic window, but it is the wrong house. You wake up at dawn curled among someone else's Christmas decorations, and you have to explain yourself to a very surprised Mr. Ferguson.
failure.art: A teenager in pajamas waking in a stranger's dusty attic among boxes of Christmas decorations, a startled man in a bathrobe peering up through the hatch

encounters.title: The Extra Room
encounters.place: Your house, in a dream
encounters.text: There is a door in the upstairs hallway that has never been there, between the bathroom and the linen closet. It is papered in flowered wallpaper from 1959. Behind it you hear a family dinner: forks on plates, laughter, a radio. Someone calls your name, warmly, to come eat before it gets cold.
encounters.art: A dim upstairs hallway in a 1980s suburban house with an extra door papered in 1959 floral wallpaper between the bathroom and the linen closet, warm light and dinner sounds leaking from under it

choices.label: Open the door and walk in

success.text: It is your bedroom from when you were six. Your old nightlight, the stuffed rabbit you lost at the county fair, the glow-in-the-dark stars on the ceiling. Nobody is eating dinner. It is just a safe place, saved for you. You sit on the little bed until you wake up.
success.art: A teenager sitting on a small child's bed in a softly lit bedroom with glow-in-the-dark stars on the ceiling, holding a worn stuffed rabbit, a nightlight glowing

failure.text: Inside is another hallway, and another door, and another. You walk through doors all night, each one papered a little older. The last door opens onto somewhere that is not your house at all, and the dinner bell rings behind you.
failure.art: An endless corridor of doors papered in progressively older wallpaper, a teenager opening the last one onto a strange dark place

choices.label: Wallpaper over the door before it opens

success.text: You find a roll of leftover wallpaper and a bucket of paste in the dream garage. Three strips, smoothed flat. The door is just a bump under the paper, then a faint outline, then nothing. The dinner sounds fade like a radio drifting off station.
success.art: A teenager smoothing a strip of wallpaper over a door in an upstairs hallway, a paste bucket and brush at their feet, the door's outline fading

failure.text: The wallpaper peels itself back off the wall in long curls. Then new doors bloom in every wall of the house, dozens of them, all papered in roses. You wake up with paste on your hands and a door-shaped bump in your bedroom wall.
failure.art: A hallway with dozens of rose-papered doors blooming from every wall, wallpaper curling off in strips, a teenager with paste-covered hands

choices.label: Knock and ask whose dinner it is

success.text: The forks go quiet. A kind, tired voice answers, "Oh. Sorry, dear, wrong house. It happens." There is a smell of pot roast and someone laughing, and the door fades into the wall like breath off a mirror.
success.art: A teenager knocking politely on a floral-papered door in a dim hallway, the door fading into the wall like breath fog, warm light dimming

failure.text: The door swings open on a long dinner table set for twelve. Every chair is empty except the one at the head, where a place card reads your name in careful cursive, and the food is still steaming.
failure.art: A long formal dinner table in a 1959 dining room set for twelve with empty chairs, a single place card with a teenager's name at the head, steaming plates

encounters.title: The Pop Quiz
encounters.place: Glimmer Falls High, in a dream
encounters.text: You are sitting in algebra in your pajamas. There is a test on your desk that you did not study for, written in an alphabet made of little teeth. The clock on the wall spins backward. The teacher at the front has no face, only a red grading pen, tapping, tapping.
encounters.art: A dreamlike high-school classroom with a teenager in pajamas at a desk, a test covered in tooth-shaped letters, a clock spinning backward, a faceless teacher tapping a red pen at the front

choices.label: Fill in every bubble with total confidence

success.text: You fill in the bubbles in a pattern that pleases you, a smiley face. The faceless teacher picks up your test, holds it up to the light, and draws a giant red A+. You wake up laughing, and for some reason you feel ready for anything.
success.art: A faceless teacher holding up a test paper with bubbles filled in to make a smiley face and a huge red A plus, a teenager in pajamas grinning

failure.text: The bubbles fill with eyes. They blink, all at once, and watch you. Every one of them follows your pencil as you try to erase. When you wake, you can still feel them, under your eyelids, blinking.
failure.art: A test paper where every answer bubble has become a blinking eye, a teenager in pajamas holding a pencil frozen above it

choices.label: Turn the test upside down, the way dreams work

success.text: Upside down, the teeth are letters. It is a crossword, and every answer is the name of one of your friends. As you write each name in, that friend walks into the classroom in their pajamas, and together you walk right out the door.
success.art: A teenager filling in a crossword test with friends' names while those friends walk into a dreamlike classroom in pajamas, the faceless teacher looking on

failure.text: Upside down, you can read it, and you wish you could not. Every question is about a secret you have never told anyone. The faceless teacher leans in close and waits for your answer.
failure.art: A faceless teacher leaning over a frightened teenager's desk, a test paper turned upside down, red pen poised

encounters.title: Saturday Morning Forever
encounters.place: Your living room carpet, in a dream
encounters.text: You are inside a Saturday morning cartoon. The colors are too bright, there is a laugh track, and you have a black outline. The Sugar Sergeant, the grinning bird from the cereal box, insists you stay for just one more episode. And one more. The episodes never end, and the bird's grin is getting wider.
encounters.art: A teenager drawn with a cartoon outline inside a brightly colored Saturday morning cartoon world, a grinning cereal-box bird mascot in a military cap looming, cartoon anvils and a canyon in the background

choices.label: Run off a cliff and just don't look down

success.text: You sprint off the edge of the canyon and keep running on thin air, legs spinning, not looking down. You run right out of the cartoon, through the TV screen and into your own bed with a squeaky sound effect. You wake up giggling.
success.art: A cartoon-outlined teenager sprinting on thin air over a deep canyon with legs blurred in a wheel, a glowing TV screen ahead of them

failure.text: You look down. There is a long, descending whistle. You hit the canyon floor in a puff of dust shaped exactly like you, and wake up on your bedroom floor with little birds circling your head.
failure.art: A teenager-shaped puff of dust at the bottom of a cartoon canyon, a dazed figure with little birds circling their head

choices.label: Wait for the commercial break and slip out

success.text: Every cartoon has a station break. You wait for the jingle, and in the half-second of black between shows, you step sideways through the edge of the screen. The Sugar Sergeant shouts "Stay tuned!" to an empty set.
success.art: A teenager stepping sideways out through the dark edge of a TV screen during a station break, a grinning cartoon bird mascot left alone on a bright set

failure.text: There are no commercials. There are no breaks. The Sugar Sergeant's grin stretches past the edges of its face. "You're our new favorite character!" it says, and the laugh track will not stop laughing.
failure.art: A cartoon cereal mascot bird with a grin stretching beyond its face, leaning over a trapped teenager, a laugh-track applause sign flashing

encounters.title: The Escalator Down
encounters.place: Starlight Mall, in a dream
encounters.text: The mall is closed, and it goes on forever. Every escalator only goes down. The same soft song plays from every speaker. Every storefront is the same orange juice stand, staffed by nobody, and the fountain at the bottom of each level is full of pennies with your face on them.
encounters.art: An infinite dreamlike shopping mall with escalators descending level after level into hazy pastel light, identical orange juice stands, a fountain filled with copper pennies, a lone teenager riding down

choices.label: Run up the down escalator

success.text: You take the steps three at a time against the current, lungs burning. Level by level you climb back up, until you burst through the food court skylight and find yourself crawling out of the ceiling of your own bedroom, onto your bed.
success.art: A teenager racing up a descending escalator in an endless pastel mall, a skylight above opening onto a bedroom ceiling

failure.text: The faster you run, the faster the escalator goes. You run all night and stay in exactly the same place, and you wake up with your legs aching as if you have run a marathon in your sleep.
failure.art: A teenager running in place on a speeding escalator in an endless mall, the steps blurring, the same storefronts sliding past again and again

choices.label: Toss a quarter in the fountain and wish to wake up

success.text: Your quarter hits the water and the whole fountain ripples outward like a bell. The pennies with your face all turn heads-up and smile. You wake with your wish granted and a handful of real coins under your pillow.
success.art: A quarter splashing into a mall fountain filled with pennies, ripples spreading like rings of light, a teenager waking with coins on their pillow

failure.text: The fountain takes your quarter, then your other quarters, then your sneakers, then pulls gently at your sleeve. You back away barefoot and wake up with your pockets empty and your feet cold.
failure.art: A mall fountain pulling at a teenager's sleeve with watery fingers, sneakers sinking among the pennies, the teen backing away barefoot

encounters.title: The Lake Comes Back
encounters.place: Crystal Street, underwater, in a dream
encounters.text: In your dream, the old Crystal Springs lake is back. Crystal Street is the bottom. Fish drift through the beams of the streetlights, your neighbor's station wagon floats past upside down, and your bike rolls slowly along the lake floor. You can breathe, somehow. Far above, moonlight wobbles on the surface.
encounters.art: A suburban cul-de-sac completely underwater at night, fish swimming through streetlight beams, a station wagon floating upside down, a teenager in pajamas suspended mid-water gazing up at moonlight rippling on the surface

choices.label: Swim hard for the moonlight on the surface

success.text: You kick hard, past the rooftops, past the TV antennas, past the top of the water tower. You break the surface with a huge gasp and wake up sitting bolt upright in bed, gulping air, completely dry and completely alive.
success.art: A teenager bursting up through the surface of a moonlit lake, water spraying, the drowned rooftops of a suburban street visible far below

failure.text: The surface keeps moving up as you swim. The moonlight gets farther, not closer. You swim until your arms give out and you wake, exhausted, with your sheets soaked through and a strand of lake weed on your pillow.
failure.art: A teenager swimming upward toward moonlight that keeps receding, a drowned street far below, lake weed drifting

choices.label: Let yourself sink and look around

success.text: On the lake floor, under the street, you see the beach that was here before: a lifeguard tower, a jukebox, kids dancing in the sand in 1955. It is not frightening. It is sad, like a song from someone else's summer. You wake knowing the town a little better.
success.art: A teenager floating near the bottom of a dream lake looking at ghostly figures of 1950s kids dancing around a jukebox on a sandy beach beside a lifeguard tower

failure.text: The bottom is soft, softer than sand, and you sink into it up to your knees, then your waist. It is warm and it does not want to let go. You wake with a gasp and find fine gray silt between your sheets.
failure.art: A teenager sinking waist-deep into soft gray silt at the bottom of a dark dream lake, bubbles rising, a drowned streetlight overhead
